definition_zh: 节俭的；节省的；精打细算的
definition_en: careful about spending money and using resources so that nothing is wasted
core_image: 一个把钱花在刀刃上、每一分都记账的人
scene: 老两口把每一分开销都记在小本子上，从不多买一样东西。My grandparents are thrifty people who record every expense and never buy anything on impulse.
sceneCN: 这里 thrifty 是「节俭的、精打细算的」（第 1 个义项：花钱谨慎、物尽其用）；句意：我的祖父母是节俭的人，每笔开销都记下来，从不冲动购物。

pos.zh: 生长茂盛的；兴旺的（旧用法）

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「节俭；节约」，也指「兴旺」；thrifty 即「有节俭之德的」
thrifty 把词尾 y 变 i 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「节俭地」
thrifty 把词尾 y 变 i 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「节俭」
thrift 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「不节俭的」

senses.title: Careful with money
senses.definition: using money and resources carefully and avoiding waste
senses.definitionCN: 谨慎使用钱财和资源、避免浪费的
senses.example: Her thrifty mother mended clothes instead of replacing them.
senses.exampleCN: 她节俭的母亲补衣服而不是换新的。
senses.why: The noun thrift first meant prosperity and later careful management of money, so the adjective thrifty came to mean governed by that careful management.
senses.whyCN: 名词 thrift 早期意为「兴旺」，后来指对钱财的用心打理，形容词 thrifty 因此表示「由这种用心打理支配的」。

senses.title: Growing well or prosperous
senses.definition: flourishing and growing strongly, used of plants and, in older English, of people and times
senses.definitionCN: 形容植物长得旺盛，旧时也形容人和时世兴旺
senses.example: Thrifty wheat grew waist high along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 河边的麦子长得齐腰高。
senses.why: The oldest sense of thrift is thriving, from the verb thrive, so a thrifty field or a thrifty household once simply meant one that prospered.
senses.whyCN: thrift 最古老的意思是「繁茂、兴旺」，来自动词 thrive，所以 thrifty 的花田或家户原先只表示「兴旺的」。

senses.title: Saving by small economies
senses.definition: designed to save money or resources through small, practical economies
senses.definitionCN: 通过细小而实际的办法来省钱或节省资源的
senses.example: They pack thrifty lunches and walk to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他们包省钱的午餐，步行上班。
senses.why: When care with money becomes a habit, it shows up as small daily practices, so the word can describe methods as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 当对钱财的在意变成习惯，就会体现在日常的小做法上，所以这个词既能形容人，也能形容做法。

intro.en: Thrifty comes from thrift, which is built on the Old Norse verb thrive, to prosper, a word that entered English during the Viking age.
intro.cn: thrifty 来自 thrift，而 thrift 由古诺尔斯语动词 thrive（兴盛）构成，这个词在维京时期进入英语。

items.en: The verb thrifask means to prosper or to thrive.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语动词 thrifask 意为「兴旺、兴盛」。

items.en: Thriven and thrive enter English, and thrift names prosperity or well being.
items.cn: thriven 与 thrive 进入英语，thrift 表示「兴旺、安好」。

items.en: Thrift shifts from prosperity to the careful management of money that makes prosperity last.
items.cn: thrift 由「兴旺」转向「使兴旺得以持续的节俭理财」。

items.en: Thrifty is formed from thrift with the adjective suffix -y.
items.cn: thrifty 由 thrift 加形容词后缀 -y 构成。

items.en: Thrifty settles on careful spending, and the older sense of flourishing survives mainly in literary writing.
items.cn: 现代英语中 thrifty 主要表示「节俭」，而「茂盛、兴旺」的旧义只在文学性文字中保留。

note.en: Thrifty is built on thrift and shares its family with thriftily and thriftiness, and in meaning it sits between economical and frugal.
note.cn: thrifty 由 thrift 构成，与 thriftily、thriftiness 同族，意义上介于 economical 与 frugal 之间。

entries.definition: the habit of saving money carefully
in a careful and saving way
the habit of being thrifty
very careful with money and food
using little money or effort
sensible and careful about money and the future

normalIntro.en: Thrifty grows out of thrift, a word for saving, and both go back to a Norse verb meaning to prosper.
normalIntro.cn: thrifty 由表示「节约」的 thrift 长出，两者都可上溯到意为「兴盛」的诺尔斯语动词。

normal.en: Thrift is the noun for saving money, and thrifty is the person who practises it.
normal.cn: thrift 是「节俭」这个名词，thrifty 就是实践节俭的人。

normal.en: Write thrift, thrifty, thriftily, and thriftiness as one family.
normal.cn: 把 thrift、thrifty、thriftily、thriftiness 作为一个词族一起记。

normal.en: Thrifty with money is a natural way to say someone spends carefully.
normal.cn: thrifty with money 是形容某人花钱谨慎的自然说法。

normal.en: Thrifty changes y to i before endings, giving thriftier and thriftiness.
normal.cn: thrifty 加词尾时把 y 变 i，得到 thriftier 与 thriftiness。

normal.en: Compare thrifty with frugal: both mean careful, but thrifty stresses saving, frugal stresses simplicity.
normal.cn: 对比 frugal：两者都指谨慎，但 thrifty 强调省钱，frugal 强调朴素简单。

abstract.en: Picture a small notebook where every coin spent is written down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小本子，每花出一枚硬币都记得清清楚楚。

abstract.en: Imagine a worn coat neatly mended instead of thrown away.
abstract.cn: 想象一件旧外套被细细缝补，而不是扔掉。

abstract.en: Think of a garden that keeps growing busily long after others wilt.
abstract.cn: 想象一座花园，在别处长势衰微之后仍不断生长。

examples.en: Thrifty families often cook at home and avoid waste.
examples.cn: 节俭的家庭常常自己做饭，避免浪费。

examples.en: She was thrifty with paper, using both sides of every sheet.
examples.cn: 她在用纸上很节省，每张纸都正反两面用。

examples.en: Growing up in a thrifty home taught him to repair rather than replace.
examples.cn: 在节俭的家庭里长大，让他学会修理而不是换新。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯里夫提」——听起来像「思路富体」，思路富、身体勤的人，花钱从不浪费；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺尔斯语 thrifask（兴盛）→ 中古英语 thrive／thrift（兴旺）→ thrift（节俭）＋后缀 -y → thrifty（节俭的；旧义「茂盛的」）。

sensesIntro.en: Thrifty begins with the Scandinavian idea of thriving, then narrows to careful saving, and finally describes the small practices that saving produces.
sensesIntro.cn: thrifty 从斯堪的纳维亚语「兴盛」的观念出发，逐步收窄为「节约」，最后又形容由节约养成的细小做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person whose ledger is full and whose waste bin is empty
core.cn: 核心意象：账本记得很满、垃圾桶却很空的人。

branches.en: Care with money is the modern everyday sense.
branches.cn: 对钱财的谨慎打理是现代日常义项。

branches.en: Thriving is the older meaning the word began with.
branches.cn: 「兴旺、茂盛」是这个词更早的起点义。

branches.en: Small economies are saving turned into everyday methods.
branches.cn: 小的节约做法是「节省」落到日常办法上的表现。

branches.en: A thrifty person and a thrifty habit share the same habit of avoiding waste.
branches.cn: 节俭的人与省钱的做法共享「避免浪费」的习惯。

branches.en: Saving carefully was once seen as the way to make a household prosper.
branches.cn: 用心省钱在旧观念里正是让家业兴旺的途径。

intro.en: Thrifty is the stem thrift with the suffix -y, and its family members change the same stem with -ly, -ness, and -less.
intro.cn: thrifty 是词干 thrift 加后缀 -y，同族的 thriftily、thriftiness、thriftless 则用 -ly、-ness、-less 改造同一词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem comes from Old Norse, not Latin, so the forms listed here are English and Scandinavian rather than Latin cognates.
latinIntro.cn: 该词干来自古诺尔斯语而非拉丁语，所以下面列出的是英语与北欧语形式，而非拉丁同源词。

items.example: Thrive and thrift share a Norse origin.
items.exampleCN: thrive 与 thrift 同出于诺尔斯语。

items.example: Thrift is the noun behind thrifty.
items.exampleCN: thrift 是 thrifty 背后的名词。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y turns thrift into thrifty.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 thrift 变成 thrifty。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms thriftily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 thriftily。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms thriftiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 thriftiness。

items.example: The suffix -less forms thriftless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 thriftless。

items.example: Thrifty describes a person or a practice.
items.exampleCN: thrifty 可形容人或做法。

items.meaning: a shop selling used goods cheaply
items.example: Thrift store keeps the saving sense in a shop name.
items.exampleCN: thrift store 把「节省」的含义保留在店名里。

items.example: The suffix -al helps build words such as economical.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 可构成 economical 这类词。

definition_zh: 激动；兴奋；使激动；使兴奋；震颤
definition_en: a sudden strong feeling of excitement and pleasure, or to make someone feel it
core_image: 胸口忽然一紧，心跳猛地提起来的一股颤栗
scene: 过山车冲到最高点后急速俯冲，女孩抓紧扶手大叫。A sudden thrill shot through her as the roller coaster dived.
sceneCN: 这里 thrill 是「一阵激动的颤栗」（第 1 个义项：强烈而伴着心跳的兴奋感）；句意：过山车俯冲时，一阵激动骤然传遍她全身。

pos.zh: 兴奋；激动；颤栗；强烈快感
使激动；使兴奋；感到颤栗

derivatives.zh: 由动词过去分词转成的形容词，义为「非常兴奋的」
由动词现在分词转成的形容词，义为「令人激动的」
thrill 加名词后缀 -er，由「刺激」转为「令人提着心的惊险作品」

senses.title: A sudden wave of excitement
senses.titleCN: 一阵强烈的兴奋与激动
senses.definition: a sudden strong feeling of excitement and pleasure, often felt in the body
senses.definitionCN: 突然涌起的强烈兴奋与快意，常伴随身体上的反应
senses.example: A thrill ran through the crowd when the singer appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 歌手一出现，一阵兴奋传遍人群。
senses.why: The Old English source means to pierce, so an emotion that pierces through the body becomes a thrill.
senses.whyCN: 古英语词源意为「刺穿」，一种「刺透」身体的情绪自然就成了激动和颤栗。

senses.title: Nervous tingling from fear
senses.titleCN: 恐惧或悬疑带来的颤栗
senses.definition: a shivery sensation caused by fear, suspense, or something uncanny
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧、悬念或怪异之物而全身发抖的感觉
senses.example: There was a thrill of fear in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他的声音里带着一丝恐惧的颤栗。
senses.why: Because piercing describes a physical shiver, the same word can name the tingling caused by dread rather than joy.
senses.whyCN: 「刺穿」描写的本是身体的发抖，所以同一个词也能指恐惧而非喜悦引起的起鸡皮疙瘩。

senses.title: Something that excites
senses.titleCN: 令人兴奋的事物；刺激源
senses.definition: an experience or activity that gives people strong excitement
senses.definitionCN: 能给人带来强烈兴奋的体验、活动或事物
senses.example: Climbing at night offers a real thrill.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里攀岩带来真正的刺激。
senses.why: The feeling is so vivid that it often stands for the whole event that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 这种感受太鲜明，于是常常直接用这个词指代产生它的整件事。

senses.title: To excite someone a lot
senses.definition: to make someone feel very happy, excited, or eager
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到非常高兴、激动或迫不及待
senses.example: The chance to visit the old town thrilled her.
senses.exampleCN: 有机会去那老城看看，让她兴奋不已。
senses.why: The noun became a verb meaning to pour this piercing excitement into someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词演变出动词，表示把这种「刺透」般的兴奋注入某人心中。

senses.title: To be delighted
senses.titleCN: 感到非常高兴；得知某事很欣然
senses.definition: to feel great pleasure and happiness about something
senses.definitionCN: 因某事而感到极大的愉快和满足
senses.example: We are thrilled to hear that the museum has reopened.
senses.exampleCN: 听说博物馆重新开放，我们非常高兴。
senses.why: The passive form of the verb, as in the phrase about being pleased, carries a calm but strong pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 动词的被动形式常表示「被高兴到了」，于是带上平静却强烈的愉快意味。

senses.title: A shiver used in medical writing
senses.titleCN: （医学语境）震颤；触摸时的细颤
senses.definition: a fine vibration or quiver that can be felt, chiefly in older medical writing
senses.definitionCN: 能感觉到的细微颤动或抖颤，多见于较早的医学文笔
senses.example: Doctors used the word to describe a faint heart quiver.
senses.exampleCN: 医生曾用这个词描述心脏轻微的颤动。
senses.why: The oldest physical sense, a quiver or vibration, survives as a rare technical use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的物理义「颤动」以罕见的技术用法残留下来，多出现在旧医学文献里。

intro.en: Thrill comes from Old English thyrelian, to pierce, and its early sense was a quiver or a piercing sensation.
intro.cn: thrill 源自古英语 thyrelian（刺穿），早期义为「颤动、被刺透般的感觉」。

items.en: Thyrelian means to pierce or make a hole through.
items.cn: thyrelian 意为刺穿或打孔穿过。

items.en: The verb thrilen names the act of piercing or boring.
items.cn: 中古英语 thrilen 指刺穿、钻透的动作。

items.en: The noun names a quiver of the body or an arrow wound.
items.cn: 名词出现，指身体的颤动或箭伤。

items.en: The meaning shifts from physical tremor to strong emotion.
items.cn: 词义由身体的震颤转向强烈的情绪。

items.en: Romantic writing links the word to delight and eager excitement.
items.cn: 浪漫主义文学让这个词与喜悦、迫不及待的兴奋相连。

items.en: The verb sense to excite and the adjective thrilled spread in both British and American use.
items.cn: 动词「使激动」与形容词 thrilled 在英美两地的用法中普及。

note.en: Thrill belongs to a small family of piercing and excitement words, and the spelling is easily confused with throw and through.
note.cn: thrill 属于由来「刺穿」引申的一端小词群，拼写上又容易与 throw 和 through 混淆。

entries.definition: very exciting
very pleased and excited
an exciting story or film
from one side or end to the other
entries.definitionCN: 从一头到另一头（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a feeling of eagerness or enthusiasm
to feel a light prickling sensation
a state of overwhelming joy

normalIntro.en: Thrill goes back to a word that means to pierce, so the feeling is something that runs through you.
normalIntro.cn: thrill 的词源本义是「刺穿」，所以这种感觉像有东西一下贯穿全身。

normal.en: The phrase the thrill of means the excitement that an activity gives.
normal.cn: 短语 the thrill of 指某项活动带来的刺激感。

normal.en: When a thrill runs through someone, excitement spreads through the body quickly.
normal.cn: 「一阵激动传遍全身」说的是兴奋迅速波及全身上下。

normal.en: To give someone a thrill is to make that person very excited.
normal.cn: to give someone a thrill 表示让某人兴奋不已。

normal.en: Thrilled is the everyday adjective for being very pleased.
normal.cn: thrilled 是日常里表示「高兴极了」的形容词。

normal.en: Thrilling describes the thing that causes excitement, while thrill describes the feeling.
normal.cn: thrilling 描述引起兴奋的事物，thrill 本身描述的则是这种感觉。

abstract.en: Picture a bookmark made of a bare strip running through a book.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细长的书簪一下穿过厚厚的书页。

abstract.en: Imagine cold water drops running down your back when you hear a strange sound.
abstract.cn: 想象听到怪响时，凉水珠顺着后背一路流下。

abstract.en: Think of a carousel ride that starts to spin faster and faster.
abstract.cn: 想象旋转木马越转越快，让人只想尖叫。

examples.en: The children were thrilled to see snow for the first time.
examples.cn: 孩子们第一次看到雪，兴奋极了。

examples.en: She felt a thrill of pride as the flag was raised.
examples.cn: 国旗升起时，她感到一阵自豪的激动。

examples.en: Nothing can match the thrill of a close race.
examples.cn: 没有什么能比得上一场势均力敌的比赛带来的刺激。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯瑞尔」——听到上台念名字那一刻，心脏「刺」地一紧，就是一阵激动；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 thyrelian（刺穿、打孔）→ 中古英语 thrilen（刺透）→ 名词义「颤动、箭伤」→ 引申为「刺透般的强烈兴奋」。核心义「一下贯穿身体的刺感」。

sensesIntro.en: Thrill moves from a piercing shiver to a wave of excitement, then to the thing that excites, and finally to the verb of exciting and the state of being delighted.
sensesIntro.cn: thrill 从「被刺穿般的颤动」发展为强烈的兴奋感，再到引起兴奋的事物，最后演变为「使激动」的动词和「非常高兴」的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tightening in the chest as the heart leaps.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸口猛地一紧，心跳陡然提起。

branches.en: A sudden wave of pleasure is the central sense.
branches.cn: 突如其来的喜悦是中心义项。

branches.en: The shiver sense flips into fear and suspense.
branches.cn: 颤栗义转向恐惧与悬念。

branches.en: The cause of excitement borrows the name of the feeling.
branches.cn: 引起兴奋的事物借用了感受之名。

branches.en: The verb and its passive both push the feeling into a person.
branches.cn: 动词及其被动形式都把这个感受推入某人心中。

branches.en: The old bodily tremor survives as a rare medical term.
branches.cn: 古老的身体颤动残留为罕见医学术语。

intro.en: Thrill is a native English root from to pierce, with thrilled, thrilling, and thriller built on it.
intro.cn: thrill 是源出「刺穿」的英语本土词根，thrilled、thrilling 与 thriller 都围绕它构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes no ancestor to thrill, but the suffix -er and the past participle ending -ed shape its family.
latinIntro.cn: thrill 没有拉丁语祖先，但名词后缀 -er 与过去分词词尾 -ed 塑造了它的词族。

items.example: Thyrelian supplies the piercing image.
items.exampleCN: thyrelian 提供「刺穿」的意象。

items.example: The Middle English verb carries the old sense.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语动词延续了古老含义。

items.example: The noun names the shiver itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词直接指那种颤动。

items.example: The verb puts the excitement into someone.
items.exampleCN: 动词表示把兴奋带给某人。

items.example: The ending -ed turns thrill into thrilled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 把 thrill 变成 thrilled。

items.example: The ending -ing forms thrilling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 thrilling。

items.meaningCN: 表示人或物的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -er forms thriller.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 thriller。

items.example: Thrilling describes exciting events.
items.exampleCN: thrilling 描述令人激动的事。

items.example: Thrilled describes a happy person.
items.exampleCN: thrilled 描述高兴的人。

definition_zh: 惊险小说；惊悚片；悬疑作品；令人紧张兴奋的事物或人
definition_en: an exciting story, film, or book, usually about crime or danger, that keeps people in suspense
core_image: 黑暗里每一步都怕踩空，手心冒汗却不肯停下
scene: 深夜读一本侦探小说，翻页时又怕又停不下。She switched off the light and refused to put down the thriller.
sceneCN: 这里 thriller 指「惊险小说」（第 1 个义项：让人一直紧绷的悬疑作品）；句意：她关了灯，却怎么也不肯放下那本惊险小说。

pos.zh: 惊险小说；惊悚片；悬疑作品

derivatives.zh: thriller 去掉后缀 -er 的基础名词，义为「一阵强烈的兴奋」
thrill 加现在分词词尾 -ing，义为「令人激动紧张的」
thrill 加过去分词词尾 -ed，义为「非常兴奋的」

senses.title: A suspenseful story or film
senses.definition: a book, film, or play with a fast, suspenseful plot, usually involving crime or danger
senses.definitionCN: 情节紧凑、充满悬念，多涉及犯罪或危险的小说、电影或戏剧
senses.example: The thriller kept me awake until two in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 那本惊险小说让我读到凌晨还没睡。
senses.why: From the nineteen twenties the word named cheap sensational fiction, because such plots were built to send a thrill through the reader.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪二十年代起，这个词指廉价的感官小说，因为那类情节就是为了让读者一阵阵发紧而写的。

senses.title: A genre label on shelves
senses.definition: the category or label under which such suspenseful works are sold or discussed
senses.definitionCN: 这类悬疑作品在售卖或讨论中所属的品类标签
senses.example: She writes in several genres, from thriller to family drama.
senses.exampleCN: 她写多种类型，从惊悚到家庭剧都有。
senses.why: Once readers learned to expect the tightening tension, the label itself became a promise of suspense.
senses.whyCN: 读者一旦习惯期待那种收紧的紧张感，这个标签本身就成了一种悬念承诺。

senses.title: The passage that makes one nervous
senses.definition: a tense scene or plot turn inside a story that produces excitement and fear at once
senses.definitionCN: 故事中让人又怕又兴奋的紧张场景或情节转折
senses.example: The chase through the tunnels is the real thriller of the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 隧道里的追逃才是整部小说真正的惊险段落。
senses.why: The name of the work can be borrowed for the single moment that delivers the strongest shock.
senses.whyCN: 作品名常被借来指代其中冲击最强的那一个片段。

senses.title: Anyone or anything that stirs suspense
senses.titleCN: 令人紧张刺激的人或事
senses.definition: a person, event, or experience that creates strong excitement and worry
senses.definitionCN: 制造强烈兴奋与不安的人、事件或经历
senses.example: The final match, decided on the last shot, was a thriller.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛最后一球才见分晓，真是一场心跳之战。
senses.why: Because -er marks the maker of the emotion, the label easily extends to anything that makes people hold their breath.
senses.whyCN: 因为后缀 -er 标记的是情绪的制造者，所以这个词很容易扩展到任何让人屏住呼吸的人或事。

intro.en: Thriller is thrill plus -er, first used for thrilling stories and plays in the late nineteenth and early twentieth century.
intro.cn: thriller 由 thrill 加后缀 -er 构成，十九世纪末至二十世纪初开始用于指令人激动的小说与戏剧。

items.en: Thyrelian means to pierce, the oldest form behind thrill.
items.cn: thyrelian 意为刺穿，是 thrill 最早的形态。

items.en: The noun thrill names a quiver of the body or a strong emotion.
items.cn: 名词 thrill 指身体的颤动或强烈的情绪。

items.en: The noun thrial is recorded in the sense of a shudder or thrill.
items.cn: 名词 thrial 有「一阵颤抖」的记载。

items.en: Thriller appears for a tale or play that produces intense excitement.
items.cn: thriller 出现，指能引起强烈兴奋的故事或戏剧。

items.en: The word is applied to detective and mystery films and novels.
items.cn: 这个词被用于侦探片、悬疑影片与小说。

items.en: Thriller becomes a standard publishing and film genre label.
items.cn: thriller 成为出版与电影业的标准类型标签。

note.en: Thriller is a -er noun meaning the thing that delivers the thrill, and it sits beside words for suspense fiction and for the felt emotion.
note.cn: thriller 是表示「带来刺激之物」的 -er 后缀名词，旁边既有悬疑作品的同类词，也有描述情绪本身的词。

entries.definition: a sudden strong feeling of excitement
very exciting
extremely pleased
something used to fill a space
entries.definitionCN: 填充物（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a story about an unsolved crime or puzzle
a feeling of tense uncertainty
a genre built to frighten

normalIntro.en: Thriller is simply thrill with -er, the suffix that points to the person or thing that makes the feeling happen.
normalIntro.cn: thriller 就是 thrill 加后缀 -er，这个词尾指向「制造这种情绪的人或物」。

normal.en: The pattern of -er is easy to see: a thriller gives a thrill, as a cleaner gives a clean.
normal.cn: -er 的构词规律很好懂：thriller 带来 thrill，正如 cleaner 带来 clean。

normal.en: A psychological thriller deals with the mind rather than loud chases.
normal.cn: psychological thriller 更侧重心理而不是喧闹的追车戏。

normal.en: A spy thriller follows agents, secrets, and narrow escapes.
normal.cn: spy thriller 围绕间谍、机密与死里逃生展开。

normal.en: The thriller genre became a standard shelf label in bookshops and cinemas.
normal.cn: the thriller genre 是书店与影院里的标准分类标签。

normal.en: Thrilled ends with d and describes a happy person, while thriller names the work.
normal.cn: thrilled 以 d 结尾，描述高兴的人；thriller 则指那部作品。

abstract.en: Picture a reader holding a torch under the bed covers at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象有人半夜钻进被窝，举着手电筒继续读。

abstract.en: Imagine a cinema audience all leaning forward at the same second.
abstract.cn: 想象全场观众在同一秒一起往前倾身。

abstract.en: Think of a door left ajar at the end of a long corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象长廊尽头有一扇虚掩的门。

examples.en: Her new thriller spent ten weeks on the bestseller list.
examples.cn: 她新写的惊险小说在畅销榜上停留了十周。

examples.en: The director is known for low-budget thrillers and tight scripts.
examples.cn: 这位导演以低成本惊悚片和紧凑剧本著称。

examples.en: Reviewers called the ending a perfect thriller twist.
examples.cn: 评论者称那个结局是完美的惊悚反转。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肆意乐」——看着主角在刀尖上走，观众却「肆意」地看得心跳加速，这正是 thriller 给人的乐趣；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 thrill（古英语 thyrelian「刺穿」→「一阵颤栗、兴奋」）+ 后缀 -er（做某事的人或物）→ thriller（制造紧张兴奋的作品）。核心义「制造刺激之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Thriller starts as a name for suspenseful stories, then becomes a genre label, a single tense passage, and finally any person or event that produces suspense.
sensesIntro.cn: thriller 先指充满悬念的故事，再成为类型标签，也可指故事里紧张的段落，最后泛指任何制造悬念的人或事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step in the dark where the floor may not hold.
core.cn: 核心意象：在黑暗中落下一步，脚下的地板也许踩空。

branches.en: The suspenseful story is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 充满悬念的故事是首要义项。

branches.en: The category label grows out of repeated reader expectation.
branches.cn: 类型标签由读者反复形成的期待长出。

branches.en: One tense passage borrows the whole name.
branches.cn: 一个紧张段落借用了整部作品的名字。

branches.en: The -er ending lets the word widen to any thrilling event.
branches.cn: -er 词尾让这个词扩展到任何激动人心的事件。

branches.en: The work and its shelf label describe the same promise of suspense.
branches.cn: 作品与它的货架标签许诺的是同一种悬念。

intro.en: Thriller is a transparent -er formation on thrill, the same suffix that makes worker or cooker.
intro.cn: thriller 是 thrill 加 -er 构成的透明派生，和 worker 或 cooker 用同一个后缀。

latinIntro.en: Neither thrill nor the suffix -er comes from Latin, so the Latin entries here are empty by design.
latinIntro.cn: thrill 与后缀 -er 都不来自拉丁语，因此这里的拉丁同源条目按规范留空。

items.example: Thyrelian is the distant source of thrill.
items.exampleCN: thyrelian 是 thrill 的遥远来源。

items.example: The noun is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的根。

items.example: Thriller is the direct result.
items.exampleCN: thriller 是直接结果。

items.meaningCN: 做某事或给出某物的人或物
items.example: The suffix -er adds the giver meaning.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 添加「给予者」的含义。

items.example: The ending -ing forms thrilling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 thrilling。

items.example: The ending -ed forms thrilled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 thrilled。

items.example: Thrilling describes the work itself.
items.exampleCN: thrilling 描述作品本身。

items.example: Thrilled describes the reader.
items.exampleCN: thrilled 描述读者。

items.example: Thrills keeps the plural idea.
items.exampleCN: thrills 保留复数概念。

definition_zh: 吞吐量；产量；处理能力；生产量
definition_en: the amount of material, data, or work that passes through a system in a given period
core_image: 原料从一头灌进机器，成品从另一头不断流出
scene: 工厂的传送带一刻不停，原料进、成品出。The plant doubled its throughput after the new line opened.
sceneCN: 这里 throughput 是「吞吐量」（第 3 个义项：一定时间内穿过系统的总量）；句意：新生产线投产后，工厂的吞吐量翻了一倍。

derivatives.zh: 意为投掷，读音与 throughput 相近，只是拼写相似，词源不同
throughput 的前半部分，义为「穿过；从头到尾」
同为 through 复合词，义为「遍及；贯穿始终」

senses.title: Goods or raw material passing through a plant
senses.definition: the quantity of raw material or goods processed by a factory or plant in a given time
senses.definitionCN: 工厂在一定时间内加工处理的原料或产品的数量
senses.example: The mill raised its grain throughput by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 这家磨坊把粮食加工量提高了三分之一。
senses.why: Through means from one end to the other, and put means placed, so throughput names what the plant puts through itself.
senses.whyCN: through 是从一端穿到另一端，put 是「放入」，于是 throughput 就是工厂「让多少东西穿过自己」。

senses.title: Volume handled by a port or carrier
senses.titleCN: 港口的货物吞吐量；运输量
senses.definition: the total volume of cargo or traffic handled by a port, road, or transport system
senses.definitionCN: 港口、道路或运输系统所处理的货物或交通总量
senses.example: The port reported record container throughput last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该港口去年集装箱吞吐量创下纪录。
senses.why: The same idea of things passing through a gateway became standard in shipping and transport reports.
senses.whyCN: 「东西穿过关口」的同一思路在航运与交通报告里成为标准说法。

senses.title: Work finished by a person or team
senses.definition: the amount of work, cases, or output a person, office, or team completes in a period
senses.definitionCN: 某个人、办公室或团队在一段时间内完成的工作量、处理件数或产出
senses.example: Nurses worry that rising throughput will cut the time spent with patients.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们担心处理量的上升会压缩与病人相处的时间。
senses.why: Jobs too can pass through a pair of hands, so throughput extends from machines to the people operating them.
senses.whyCN: 活计同样会从一双手里穿过，所以吞吐量从机器扩展到操作机器的人身上。

senses.title: Data moving through a system
senses.definition: the rate at which data is sent, received, or processed by a computer network or device
senses.definitionCN: 计算机网络或设备发送、接收或处理数据的速率
senses.example: The new router achieves far higher throughput on busy networks.
senses.exampleCN: 新路由器在繁忙网络中的吞吐量高得多。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the factory image: bits flow through cables and chips as grain flowed through mills.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了工厂的意象：比特流穿过线缆与芯片，正如谷物穿过磨坊。

senses.title: Overall capacity of a system
senses.definition: the general capacity of any system to take input, process it, and produce results
senses.definitionCN: 任何系统接受输入、加工并产出结果的总体能力
senses.example: The lab added staff to increase the overall throughput of tests.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室增加了人手，以提高检测的总体处理能力。
senses.why: When the image is abstracted into input and output, throughput becomes a general measure of capacity.
senses.whyCN: 当这一意象被抽象成输入与产出，throughput 就成了衡量处理能力的通用指标。

intro.en: Throughput combines through with put, both native English words, and appears as a technical term in the early twentieth century.
intro.cn: throughput 由 through 与 put 两个英语本土词复合而成，二十世纪初作为技术术语出现。

items.en: Thurh means through, and potian or putian carries the sense of putting.
items.cn: 古英语 thurh 意为「穿过」，potian 或 putian 带有「放置」之意。

items.en: Through settles as a spelling, and put is used for placing something.
items.cn: 中古英语里 through 的拼写逐渐固定，put 用于表示「放置」。

items.en: Through- compounds grow common in engineering and railway language.
items.cn: 十九世纪，以 through 开头的复合词在工程与铁路用语中开始流行。

items.en: Throughput is recorded for material passing through a plant or process.
items.cn: throughput 被用于指工厂或工序中流过的物料。

items.en: The term spreads to transport, medicine, and management writing.
items.cn: 这个词扩散到运输、医学与管理写作中。

items.en: Computing makes throughput a key measure of network speed.
items.cn: 计算机领域让 throughput 成为衡量网络速度的关键指标。

note.en: Throughput is a compound of through and put, close in shape to output and to throw, and close in meaning to capacity words.
note.cn: throughput 是 through 与 put 的复合词，形近于 output 和 throw，意思上又靠近表示「能力」的同类词。

entries.definition: the amount produced
what is put into a system
from one end or side to the other
past tense of throw
entries.definitionCN: throw 的过去式（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the maximum amount a system can hold or handle
the amount produced by land or effort
the data capacity of a connection

normalIntro.en: Throughput is literally what is put through: count the items that go in one end and come out the other.
normalIntro.cn: throughput 字面就是「被put through的东西」：数一数从一头进、从另一头出的货物数量。

normal.en: Split it into put and through, and the meaning becomes clear at once.
normal.cn: 把它拆成两部分，put 加 through，意思一下就清楚了。

normal.en: High throughput is a compliment for a factory or a server.
normal.cn: high throughput 是对工厂或服务器的夸奖。

normal.en: Network throughput measures how fast data passes through a connection.
normal.cn: network throughput 衡量数据通过一条连接的快慢。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with output: output is what comes out, throughput is what passes all the way through.
normal.cn: 别和 output 混淆：output 强调出来的产物，throughput 强调一路穿过的总量。

normal.en: The plural throughputs appears in technical reports about several systems.
normal.cn: 复数 throughputs 出现在同时比较多个系统的技术报告里。

abstract.en: Picture a mill wheel turning while sacks of grain keep arriving.
abstract.cn: 想象磨坊的水轮不停转动，粮袋源源不断地送来。

abstract.en: Imagine one door of a ship where boxes enter and leave without pause.
abstract.cn: 想象船上一扇门，箱子不停地进进出出。

abstract.en: Think of a pipe that is never once empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一根永远不会空下来的管道。

examples.en: Engineers measured the throughput of the new pipeline over a month.
examples.cn: 工程师们用一个月时间测量了新管道的输送吞吐量。

examples.en: Low throughput at the clinic means longer waiting times.
examples.cn: 诊所处理量低，意味着等候时间更长。

examples.en: The team tuned the software to raise data throughput.
examples.cn: 团队调整了软件，以提高数据吞吐量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「丝入铺特」——原料像丝线一样源源「入」厂、铺满传送带，出去的数量就是吞吐量；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 through（穿过；从头到尾）+ put（放入）→ throughput，指在单位时间内「放进去穿过」某系统的东西总量。核心义「流过系统的总量」。

sensesIntro.en: Throughput begins with material flowing through a plant, spreads to ports and work, then to data, and finally becomes a general measure of system capacity.
sensesIntro.cn: throughput 从工厂里流过的物料开始，扩展到港口与工作处理量，再到数据传输量，最后成为衡量系统能力的通用指标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grain poured in at one end, flour streaming out at the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：谷物从一端倒进去，面粉从另一端不断流出。

branches.en: Factory processing is the earliest recorded sense.
branches.cn: 工厂处理量是最早有记录的含义。

branches.en: Ports and carriers count what passes their gates.
branches.cn: 港口与运输方统计穿过关口的东西。

branches.en: People and offices also handle cases faster or slower.
branches.cn: 人与办公室处理事务也有快慢之别。

branches.en: Data is treated as material flowing through cables.
branches.cn: 数据被当成流经线缆的物料。

branches.en: Concrete flow becomes an abstract measure of capacity.
branches.cn: 具体的流动最终抽象为衡量能力的指标。

intro.en: Throughput is a compound, not an affixed word: through and put join as two complete English words.
intro.cn: throughput 是复合词而非前后缀派生词，through 与 put 是两个完整的英语词拼接而成。

latinIntro.en: Both elements of throughput are native English, so no Latin entries are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: throughput 的两个成分都是英语本土词，因此这里不列拉丁同源条目。

items.meaning: from one end to the other
items.example: Through gives the crossing idea.
items.exampleCN: through 提供「穿过」的意象。

items.example: Put supplies the placing idea.
items.exampleCN: put 提供「放入」的含义。

items.example: The compound names the total passing through.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指穿过系统的总量。

items.example: The plural compares separate systems.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式用于比较不同系统。

items.example: Output shares the second element.
items.exampleCN: output 共享后半部分成分。

items.example: Input is the mirror compound.
items.exampleCN: input 是对应的反向复合词。

items.meaning: in every part, all the way
items.example: Throughout shares the through element.
items.exampleCN: throughout 共享 through 成分。

items.meaning: a road going right through a place
items.example: Throughway shows how through builds nouns.
items.exampleCN: throughway 展示 through 如何构成名词。

definition_zh: 重击；砰然一声；使砰然作响；重拳；怦怦直跳
definition_en: to hit something heavily and with a dull sound, or such a heavy blow or the dull sound it makes
core_image: 拳头落在木门上，一声闷响，门板跟着颤了一下
scene: 宿舍门口，一个男生抬手重重敲了几下门，声音闷闷的。He thumped on the door with the flat of his hand.
sceneCN: 这里 thump 是「重击、发出闷响」（第 1 个义项：用钝力重重地打并发出沉闷声）；句意：他用巴掌重重拍门。

pos.zh: 重击；砰然作响；使发出闷响

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转形容词，义为「巨大的、极大的」，也作动词的现在分词
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「重击者；声音沉重的东西」

senses.title: To hit heavily with a dull sound
senses.definition: to strike something with a heavy blow that makes a dull, deep sound
senses.definitionCN: 用沉重的力道击打某物，发出低沉钝闷的声音
senses.example: He thumped the table with his fist.
senses.exampleCN: 他用拳头重重捶了一下桌子。
senses.why: The word is imitative of the dull sound itself, so the blow and its noise arrive together.
senses.whyCN: 这个词模仿击打时那种沉闷的声响，所以「打」和「响」是同时出现的。

senses.title: To beat or pound as a heart does
senses.definition: to beat strongly and heavily, especially in fear or excitement
senses.definitionCN: 尤指因恐惧或激动而剧烈、沉重地跳动
senses.example: Her heart was thumping as she climbed onto the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 她登上舞台时心怦怦直跳。
senses.why: A heart beating hard sounds like a fist knocking, so the physical thump is moved inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 心脏剧烈跳动听起来像有人用拳头叩门，于是外在的闷响被移到了身体内部。

senses.title: The dull sound of a heavy fall
senses.definition: a low, dull noise made when something heavy falls or lands
senses.definitionCN: 重物落地或撞击时发出的低沉钝响
senses.example: The book landed on the floor with a thump.
senses.exampleCN: 书砰的一声掉在地板上。
senses.why: As a noun the word becomes the sound itself, which is how we hear a heavy fall before we see it.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词就成了声音本身——沉重落地时，我们往往先听见那一声，才看见东西。

senses.title: A heavy blow from a fist
senses.definition: a heavy punch or hit, especially one delivered with a fist
senses.definitionCN: 沉重的一拳或一击，尤指用拳头打出的
senses.example: He gave the driver a thump on the shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 他在司机肩上重重拍了一拳。
senses.why: The sound name is lent to the kinds of blows that make it, so the noun also means the hit itself.
senses.whyCN: 能发出这种闷响的击打，自然也可以用这个词来称呼，于是名词也指「那一拳」本身。

senses.title: To place or sit down heavily
senses.titleCN: 重重地放下；一屁股坐下
senses.definition: to put something down or sit down with force, often as if dropping
senses.definitionCN: 用力地把东西放下或坐下，常常像顺势一丢
senses.example: She thumped the bag down on the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 她把包重重地扔在长椅上。
senses.why: Dropping a heavy object also makes the dull knock, so thump widens from striking to setting down.
senses.whyCN: 重物放下也会砸出闷响，所以 thump 从「击打」扩展到「重重放下」。

intro.en: Thump is generally explained as an imitative word, a sixteenth-century English coinage shaped after the dull sound it names.
intro.cn: thump 一般认为属于拟声词，是十六世纪英语靠模仿沉闷声响造出来的词。

items.en: The form follows the dull sound of a fist or heavy object, a common pattern in English.
items.cn: 词的形态模仿拳头或重物砸下的闷响，这在英语里很常见。

items.en: Thump appears in English writing in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: thump 在十六世纪的英语书面材料中开始出现。

items.en: Early use covers both the heavy blow and the dull sound it makes.
items.cn: 早期用法同时涵盖「重击」和它发出的闷响。

items.en: The sense of a heart pounding appears in writing in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 「心脏怦怦跳」的义项在十八世纪的书面语中出现。

items.en: Modern English extends thump to footsteps, music, and heavy machinery.
items.cn: 现代英语把 thump 扩展到脚步声、音乐和重型机械的震动。

note.en: Thump is the family of heavy dull sounds, close to thud, bump, and bang, and to the lighter tap and knock.
note.cn: thump 属于「沉闷重响」一族，与 thud、bump、bang 相邻，也与较轻的 tap、knock 形成对照。

entries.definition: huge, very large; also the present participle of thump
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的；也可作 thump 的现在分词

entries.definition: someone or something that thumps
entries.definitionCN: 重击的人或发出闷响的东西

entries.definition: a dull sound like a heavy object hitting a surface
entries.definitionCN: 重物砸在表面上的闷响；只是拼写与声响相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to hit something many times with great force
to hit something noisily, or such a loud sharp noise
entries.definitionCN: 砰地敲打；响声更尖更响

entries.definition: to hit a door or surface to attract attention
entries.definitionCN: 敲（门）；力度较轻且通常有节奏

normalIntro.en: Thump sounds like what it does: the spelling traces a heavy blow and the dull answer it gets back.
normalIntro.cn: thump 的声音本身就是它的意思：拼写描出一记重击，以及它换来的一声闷响。

normal.en: Thump is imitative, so say it aloud with a downward punch and you will hear the dull thud.
normal.cn: thump 是拟声词，念的时候配上向下的一拳，就能听见那声闷响。

normal.en: The -ing form gives the adjective thumping, as in a thumping majority.
normal.cn: 加 -ing 构成形容词 thumping，例如「压倒性的多数」。

normal.en: Thump on the door is a rougher, heavier version of knock on the door.
normal.cn: thump on the door 是 knock on the door 更粗重、更用力的版本。

normal.en: Your heart thumps when you are nervous; no one makes a sound, yet the beat is like a drum.
normal.cn: 紧张时心会 thump；没人发出声音，可心跳却像敲鼓。

normal.en: Compare thud: a thud is a body or object landing, a thump is usually a blow being delivered.
normal.cn: 对比 thud：thud 多是身体或物体落地，thump 多是有人主动打出的一击。

abstract.en: Picture a fist hitting a wooden door and the door trembling.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头砸上木门，门板跟着颤了一下。

abstract.en: Picture a chest rising and falling with a drum-like beat under the shirt.
abstract.cn: 想象一件衬衫下面有一面鼓，随着心跳一起一伏。

abstract.en: Picture a thick dictionary sliding off a desk and hitting the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚词典从桌上滑落，咚的一声砸在地板上。

examples.en: The children thumped up the stairs in their boots.
examples.cn: 孩子们穿着靴子咚咚地跑上楼。

examples.en: He was so angry that he thumped the table and walked out.
examples.cn: 他气得猛捶桌子，然后走了出去。

examples.en: We heard a loud thump and ran to the window.
examples.cn: 我们听到一声闷响，就赶紧跑到窗边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「桑普」——像打桩机砸下去时的那声闷响，砸一下就是重击；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为属拟声词：英语模仿击打时沉闷的「砰、咚」声构成 thump（约十六世纪），既指重击也指闷响；来源不确定，不与拉丁词根挂钩。

sensesIntro.en: Thump starts as the dull sound of a heavy blow and spreads to the beating heart, the sound of a fall, the blow itself, and setting things down hard.
sensesIntro.cn: thump 从「重击发出的闷响」出发，延伸到心脏怦怦跳、重物落地之声、那记拳脚本身，以及把东西重重放下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fist landing on a wooden door with a dull knock.
core.cn: 核心意象：拳头砸在木门上，咚地一声闷响。

branches.en: The core action: hitting hard so that the blow sounds dull.
branches.cn: 核心动作：用力砸下去，声音发闷。

branches.en: The beating heart borrows the same drum-like knock.
branches.cn: 心跳借用同样如鼓的叩击感。

branches.en: The noise itself becomes a noun for a heavy fall.
branches.cn: 那声响本身成了名词，指重物落地。

branches.en: The name of the sound is given to the fist blow that makes it.
branches.cn: 发出这种声音的拳头一击，也被直接用这个词称呼。

branches.en: Striking, landing, and setting down all produce the same dull thump.
branches.cn: 击打、落地、放下都会发出同样沉闷的一声。

intro.en: Thump is an imitative base word; its family is built with English endings such as -ing and -er rather than Latin pieces.
intro.cn: thump 是拟声词根，词族靠英语后缀 -ing、-er 构成，而不是拉丁构件。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is known for thump, so the Latin entries are left empty and only English forms are listed.
latinIntro.cn: thump 没有可靠的拉丁语来源，因此拉丁同源条留空，只列英语形式。

items.meaning: a heavy blow with a dull sound
items.example: Thump is the base verb and noun.
items.exampleCN: thump 是可作动词也可作名词的基础词。

items.example: The drum thumps and the crowd cheers.
items.exampleCN: 鼓声咚咚作响，人群欢呼。

items.meaning: past tense and past participle of thump
items.meaningCN: thump 的过去式和过去分词
items.example: He thumped the wall twice.
items.exampleCN: 他在墙上重重敲了两下。

items.meaning: huge; or the act of thumping
items.meaningCN: 巨大的；或敲击这一动作
items.example: They won by a thumping margin.
items.exampleCN: 他们以压倒性的优势获胜。

items.example: The old engine was a real thumper.
items.exampleCN: 那台老发动机响得咚咚作响。

items.meaningCN: 数下沉重的敲击或闷响
items.example: The thumps from upstairs woke me.
items.exampleCN: 楼上咚咚的响声把我吵醒了。

items.meaning: a dull sound of a heavy fall
items.example: Thud is a related sound word with a similar shape.
items.exampleCN: thud 是形态相近的相关拟声词。

items.example: Bump shares the same imitative family.
items.exampleCN: bump 与它同属拟声词一组。

definition_zh: 雷雨云；积雨云；阴沉的乌云
definition_en: a large dark cloud that produces thunder and lightning, the kind seen in a severe storm
core_image: 午后天空耸起一座黑灰色的云塔，内部一闪一闪，像压着怒火
scene: 暴雨来临前，天空从晴蓝转成铅灰，远处云层里亮起闪光。A huge thundercloud was rolling in from the west, its base almost black.
sceneCN: 这里 thundercloud 是「雷雨云」（第 1 个义项：产生雷电的大块乌云）；句意：一大团雷雨云正从西边压过来，云底几乎是黑的。

derivatives.zh: thundercloud 的复数形式，义为「一片片雷雨云」
由 thunder 与 head 复合而成，指雷雨云顶部高耸膨胀的部分

senses.title: A storm cloud that makes thunder
senses.definition: a very large, dark cloud in which lightning forms and thunder is heard
senses.definitionCN: 巨大而乌黑的云，里面有闪电生成，并可听见雷声
senses.example: The thundercloud grew darker as the storm approached.
senses.exampleCN: 随着暴风雨逼近，雷雨云越来越黑。
senses.why: The compound simply joins the sound of thunder to the cloud that carries it, so the name says exactly what the cloud does.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词只是把「雷声」和「承载雷声的云」拼在一起，名字本身就说明了云的功能。

senses.title: The technical term cumulonimbus
senses.definition: the meteorological name for a tall cumulus cloud that produces lightning and heavy rain
senses.definitionCN: 气象学中对产生闪电与大雨的高耸积状云的正式称呼
senses.example: Meteorologists classify it as cumulonimbus, known in plain language as a thundercloud.
senses.exampleCN: 气象学家把它归为积雨云，日常说法就是雷雨云。
senses.why: Science needed a precise label for the same object, so thundercloud became the everyday mirror of the Latin term cumulonimbus.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要对同一对象给出精确名称，于是雷雨云成了拉丁词 cumulonimbus 的日常说法。

senses.title: A dark mass that looks stormy
senses.definition: any heavy dark cloud that makes a sky look threatening, even if no thunder follows
senses.definitionCN: 任何沉重乌黑、让天色变得压抑的云，即使最后并没有打雷
senses.example: Rows of thunderclouds hung over the harbour all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 整个上午海港上方都挂着成片的乌云。
senses.why: Once the word stands for the dark look of a storm sky, speakers use it for threatening clouds that never actually thunder.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词代表暴风雨天空的暗色外观，人们就会用它形容那些看起来阴沉、却最终没有打雷的云。

senses.title: The raging inner storm of a face
senses.definition: a dark, angry look on a face, as if a storm were about to break
senses.definitionCN: 脸上阴沉愠怒的神情，仿佛马上要爆发一场风暴
senses.example: A thundercloud crossed his face when he heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 他一听到这个消息，脸立刻阴沉下来。
senses.why: Since a thundercloud announces an approaching storm, the same image transfers to a person about to erupt in anger.
senses.whyCN: 雷雨云预示着风暴将至，同样的画面就转用到即将发怒的人脸上。

intro.en: Thundercloud is a native English compound: the noun thunder plus the noun cloud, both of which go back to Old and Middle English.
intro.cn: thundercloud 是英语本土复合词，由名词 thunder 与名词 cloud 组成，两部分都可追溯到古英语或中古英语。

items.en: Thunor names the god and the rumble of the sky, the source of modern thunder.
items.cn: thunor 既指雷神，也指天上的轰鸣，是现代 thunder 的来源。

items.en: Clud means a mass of rock; only later does the word shift to the clouds in the sky.
items.cn: clud 本指岩块，后来才转指天空中的云。

items.en: Spellings settle into thunder and cloud, and compounds such as thunderbolt are already in use.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，拼写定型为 thunder 与 cloud，thunderbolt 一类复合词也已在用。

items.en: Thundercloud is recorded in the sense of a storm-producing cloud as weather writing grows.
items.cn: 随着气象记述的增多，thundercloud 以「产生雷雨的云」之义被记录下来。

items.en: Modern science pairs the everyday word with cumulonimbus, and the word is also used in figurative descriptions of anger.
items.cn: 现代科学把这一日常词与积雨云并称，这个词也被用来比喻怒色。

note.en: Thundercloud is a compound in the storm family, close in form to thunderbolt and thunderstorm and in meaning to storm cloud, cumulonimbus, and overcast.
note.cn: thundercloud 是「风暴家族」的复合词，形式上与 thunderbolt、thunderstorm 相邻，语义上与 storm cloud、cumulonimbus、overcast 相邻。

entries.definition: a storm with thunder and lightning
entries.definitionCN: 带雷电的暴风雨；同用 thunder 构词，但整体指风暴

entries.definition: a flash of lightning together with the thunder that follows it
the swelling upper part of a storm cloud
entries.definitionCN: 雷雨云顶部膨胀高耸的部分

entries.definition: the scientific name for a towering storm cloud
entries.definitionCN: 积雨云；气象学中对雷雨云的正式称谓

entries.definition: a dark cloud from which a storm may come
entries.definitionCN: 风暴云；可能带来暴风雨的乌云，范围比雷雨云更宽

entries.definition: covered with grey cloud so that the sky is dull
entries.definitionCN: 阴天的；满天灰云的，强调天色而非单个云团

normalIntro.en: Thundercloud is built straight from two familiar words, which makes the meaning easy to keep in mind.
normalIntro.cn: thundercloud 直接用两个熟悉的词拼成，意思一目了然。

normal.en: Thunder plus cloud: the cloud that carries thunder is drawn out by its own name.
normal.cn: thunder 加 cloud：会打雷的那团云，名字已经把它画了出来。

normal.en: The plural thunderclouds suits skies full of them, as in thunderclouds gathering over the hills.
normal.cn: 复数 thunderclouds 适合成片的云，例如山冈上空聚集的雷雨云。

normal.en: Compare thunderhead, which names only the swollen top of such a cloud.
normal.cn: 对比 thunderhead：它只指这类云顶部膨胀的部分。

normal.en: In weather reports the same thing is called cumulonimbus, so you get two names for one object.
normal.cn: 天气预报里同一样东西叫积雨云，所以一个对象有两个名字。

normal.en: Thunderstorm is the whole event, while a thundercloud is the single object in the sky.
normal.cn: thunderstorm 指整个天气过程，thundercloud 指天空中那一团云。

abstract.en: Picture a grey tower of cloud rising over a flat field, lit from within.
abstract.cn: 想象一片平地上方升起一座灰云塔，内部透着光。

abstract.en: Picture a face going dark before someone shouts, the way a sky goes dark before rain.
abstract.cn: 想象有人正要发火前脸先沉下来，就像下雨前的天空先变暗。

abstract.en: Picture the black base of a cloud hugging a hilltop.
abstract.cn: 想象一团云的黑色底部紧贴着山顶。

examples.en: A single thundercloud can hold millions of litres of water.
examples.cn: 一朵雷雨云可以蓄积数百万升的水。

examples.en: Pilots avoid flying through a thundercloud because of turbulence and ice.
examples.cn: 飞行员会避开穿越雷雨云，因为那里有湍流和结冰。

examples.en: The last thunderclouds moved east and the sun came out again.
examples.cn: 最后的几片雷雨云向东移去，太阳又出来了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「散的 + 克劳德」——乌云散开之后雷声随之而来，听见闷响就知道云在头顶；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土复合词：thunder（古英语 thunor，雷声；与雷神之名同源）+ cloud（古英语 clud 岩块，后转指云），合起来即「会打雷的云」。

sensesIntro.en: Thundercloud names the storm cloud itself, then its scientific label, then any dark stormy cloud, and finally a metaphor for an angry face.
sensesIntro.cn: thundercloud 先指那团会打雷的云，再指它的科学名称，然后泛指任何阴沉乌云，最后比喻发怒的脸色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark tower of cloud with light flickering inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座黑沉的云塔，内部不时亮起闪光。

branches.en: The plain name for the cloud that produces thunder.
branches.cn: 对「会打雷的云」的朴素称呼。

branches.en: The scientific label cumulonimbus names the same object.
branches.cn: 科学名称「积雨云」指的是同一样东西。

branches.en: The dark look of the cloud stretches to threatening skies without thunder.
branches.cn: 云的暗色外观被扩展到没有雷声的阴沉天象。

branches.en: The storm image moves from the sky to a person on the point of anger.
branches.cn: 风暴意象从天空移到即将发怒的人身上。

branches.en: All three share one picture: something heavy, dark, and about to break.
branches.cn: 这三者共享同一画面：沉重、昏暗、即将爆发。

intro.en: Thundercloud is a compound of two native English nouns, both nouns coming from Old English and reshaped through Middle English.
intro.cn: thundercloud 由两个英语本土名词复合而成，两者都源自英语的古英语阶段，并经过中古英语改造。

latinIntro.en: The parts of thundercloud are Germanic rather than Latin, so its Latin entries are left empty and only Old English forms are listed.
latinIntro.cn: thundercloud 的构件属于日耳曼语词源，而非拉丁语，因此拉丁同源条留空，只列古英语形式。

items.meaning: the loud sound that follows lightning
items.example: Thunder warns of an approaching storm.
items.exampleCN: 雷声预告暴风雨将临。

items.meaning: a mass of visible water vapour
items.example: The cloud blocked the sun.
items.exampleCN: 那片云遮住了太阳。

items.example: Thunor is the Old English ancestor of thunder.
items.exampleCN: thunor 是 thunder 的古英语祖形。

items.meaning: a rock or mound, later a cloud
items.example: Clud shifted from stone to sky.
items.exampleCN: clud 的含义从石头转向了天空。

items.example: The thunderstorm knocked out the power.
items.exampleCN: 雷暴导致停电。

items.meaning: the swollen top of a storm cloud
items.example: The thunderhead rose over the plain.
items.exampleCN: 雷雨云顶部在平原上升起。

items.example: A thunderbolt struck the oak tree.
items.exampleCN: 一道霹雳击中了那棵橡树。

items.example: The suffix -y makes thundery from thunder.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 thunder 变成 thundery。

items.example: The air felt close and thundery.
items.exampleCN: 空气闷得让人预感到雷雨。

definition_zh: 胳肢；发痒；使高兴；逗乐；觉得有意思
definition_en: to touch someone lightly so that they laugh or feel a tingling sensation, or to please and amuse someone
core_image: 一根羽毛沿着手臂轻轻扫过，皮肤一颤，人忍不住笑出声
scene: 周末午后，妈妈把手指伸进孩子的衣领，轻轻挠了几下。The little girl giggled as her father tickled her under the chin.
sceneCN: 这里 tickle 是「胳肢、轻挠」（第 1 个义项：轻轻触碰让人发笑或发痒）；句意：爸爸挠小女孩的下巴，逗得她咯咯直笑。

pos.zh: 胳肢；使发痒；使高兴；逗乐

collocations.zh: 合你心意；引起你的兴趣

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ish 构成，义为「怕痒的」，也引申指「棘手、须小心对付的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「提醒本、备忘便条」，也指挠痒的人或物
由现在分词转形容词，义为「发痒的」，也可作名词指「挠痒」

senses.title: To touch lightly so that someone laughs
senses.definition: to move your fingers lightly over parts of someone body, such as the sides or the neck, so that they laugh or squirm
senses.definitionCN: 用手指轻轻划过别人身体的某些部位，如两侧或脖子，使对方发笑或扭动
senses.example: He tickled his baby sister until she laughed.
senses.exampleCN: 他胳肢小妹妹，直到她笑起来。
senses.why: The core image is a light moving touch, and the lightest place for it is the skin, where it turns into laughter.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是「轻快地触摸」，最轻的落点就是皮肤，而皮肤上的轻触会变成笑声。

senses.title: To give a tingling itch
senses.definition: to cause a slight, tingling feeling in the throat, nose, or skin
senses.definitionCN: 使喉咙、鼻子或皮肤产生轻微刺痒的感觉
senses.example: Dust tickled my nose until I sneezed.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘弄得我鼻子发痒，一直打喷嚏。
senses.why: A tickle and an itch are the same faint tingle in the skin, so the verb also means causing that slight irritation.
senses.whyCN: 「挠痒」和「发痒」是皮肤上同一种若有若无的刺感，因此这个词也指叫人轻微难受的刺痒。

senses.title: To amuse and please someone
senses.definition: to please, amuse, or interest someone in a light and enjoyable way
senses.definitionCN: 以轻松愉快的方式使某人高兴、发笑或产生兴趣
senses.example: The story tickled the children so much that they asked for more.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事太逗了，孩子们听了还要听。
senses.why: Laughter produced by light fingers becomes the picture of delight, so anything mildly pleasing can tickle a person.
senses.whyCN: 手指轻挠带来的笑，成了表达「愉悦」的画面，任何让人开心的小事都能 tickle 一个人。

senses.title: To stir interest or curiosity
senses.definition: to attract interest, curiosity, or taste in a playful way, often in fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 以俏皮的方式引起兴趣、好奇或好感，常用于固定短语中
senses.example: The idea of a trip to the coast tickled her fancy.
senses.exampleCN: 去海边旅行这个念头让她动了心。
senses.why: The same light touch can stir the mind, so tickle extends from the skin to curiosity and taste.
senses.whyCN: 同样的轻触既能拨动皮肤，也能拨动心思，所以 tickle 从皮肤扩展到了好奇与喜好。

senses.title: A tickling sensation or act
senses.definition: a slight tingling feeling, or the playful act of tickling someone
senses.definitionCN: 轻微的痒感，或嬉闹地挠人痒痒的行为
senses.example: She gave the puppy a friendly tickle behind the ears.
senses.exampleCN: 她友好地挠了挠小狗耳后。
senses.why: As a noun the word names the sensation itself and the playful action that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，它既指那种痒痒的感觉，也指引发这种感觉的嬉闹动作。

intro.en: Tickle is an English word of uncertain origin, generally taken as imitative of light scratching or tingling; the Middle English form is tikelen.
intro.cn: tickle 是来源不确定的英语词，一般认为模仿轻挠或刺痒的感觉；中古英语形式为 tikelen。

items.en: The word is not traced to Latin or Greek; several short forms with a k sound cluster in it, and imitative origin is often suggested.
items.cn: 这个词不能追溯到拉丁语或希腊语；与之相近的一批短词都带着 k 音，所以常被认为有拟声来源。

items.en: Tikelen means to touch lightly so as to make someone laugh.
items.cn: 中古英语 tikelen 意为轻触某人使其发笑。

items.en: A related form also names a light itch or tingle of the skin.
items.cn: 相关形式也指皮肤上轻微的痒或刺感。

items.en: The spelling settles as tickle, and the pleasing sense grows alongside the physical one.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐定型为 tickle，「使人愉快」的用法与身体动作的用法一同发展。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as tickle someone pink and tickle your fancy appear, along with the adjective ticklish.
items.cn: 于是出现了「tickle someone pink」这类固定说法和形容词 ticklish。

note.en: Tickle is a light, playful touch, close in form to its own family ticklish and tickler, and in meaning to itch, amuse, and titillate.
note.cn: tickle 是一种轻巧、带玩闹性的触碰，形式上与词族 ticklish、tickler 相邻，语义上与 itch、amuse、titillate 相邻。

entries.definition: easily tickled, or needing careful handling
entries.definitionCN: 怕痒的；也指棘手需小心处理的

entries.definition: a memo or reminder list, or something that tickles
entries.definitionCN: 提醒便条、备忘本；也指挠痒的人或物

entries.definition: a tiny mark such as a dot over a letter
entries.definitionCN: 字母上的小点等微小记号；只是拼写相似，词源不同

entries.definition: to have a feeling on the skin that makes you want to scratch
entries.definitionCN: 发痒；痒得想挠，强调需要缓解的不适

entries.definition: to make someone laugh or pass the time pleasantly
entries.definitionCN: 逗乐；使消遣，语气比 tickle 更中性

entries.definition: to excite someone pleasantly, often in a slight or teasing way
entries.definitionCN: 使兴奋、逗引，正式用语，常含轻微撩拨之意

normalIntro.en: Tickle is all about a light, quick touch, and its word family carries the same playful feel.
normalIntro.cn: tickle 的核心就是又快又轻的一碰，它的词族也带着同样的玩闹感。

normal.en: Add -ish and you get ticklish, the state of being easily tickled, which also describes a delicate problem.
normal.cn: 加上 -ish 得到 ticklish，表示「怕痒」，也用来形容棘手的问题。

normal.en: Tickle someone pink is a set phrase meaning to make them very happy.
normal.cn: tickle someone pink 是固定说法，意为把某人逗得开心极了。

normal.en: Tickle your fancy means to appeal to your taste, as in the menu tickled my fancy.
normal.cn: tickle your fancy 表示「合你心意」，例如菜单上的东西让她动了心。

normal.en: The throat can tickle too, and a tickle in the throat is a familiar cough warning.
normal.cn: 喉咙也会 tickle，喉咙发痒常是咳嗽的前兆。

normal.en: Compare itch: an itch makes you need to scratch, while a tickle usually makes you laugh.
normal.cn: 对比 itch：itch 让人非挠不可，tickle 通常让人发笑。

abstract.en: Picture a feather drawn slowly along a forearm and the small shake that follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一根羽毛沿小臂缓缓扫过，随后是一下轻轻的抖。

abstract.en: Picture a speck of dust drifting up a nostril and the sudden sneeze.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒灰尘飘进鼻孔，然后猛地一声喷嚏。

abstract.en: Picture people laughing at a clever joke until they cannot stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人被一个俏皮笑话逗得停不下来。

examples.en: My feet are so ticklish that I cannot bear being tickled.
examples.cn: 我的脚特别怕痒，一被挠就受不了。

examples.en: The smell of pepper tickled his nose and made him sneeze.
examples.cn: 胡椒的气味让他鼻子发痒，打了个喷嚏。

examples.en: I was tickled to hear that you won the prize.
examples.cn: 听说你得了奖，我特别高兴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提扣」——手指轻轻一「提」，再一「扣」在腰侧，人就痒得直笑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 tikelen（轻挠使发笑），来源不确定，一般认为属拟声词，模仿轻挠或刺痒的细微感觉；另有形近词族 ticklish、tickler。

sensesIntro.en: Tickle moves from fingers making someone laugh, to a tingling urge in the skin, to amusing a person, to stirring their interest, and finally to the sensation or act itself.
sensesIntro.cn: tickle 从「用手指挠得人发笑」开始，依次扩展到皮肤上的刺痒、使人高兴、激起兴趣，最后指痒感或挠痒本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a feather grazing the skin and a sudden laugh.
core.cn: 核心意象：羽毛扫过皮肤，人忍不住笑出来。

branches.en: The core act: light fingers on ribs or neck bringing laughter.
branches.cn: 核心动作：手指轻挠肋旁或脖子，引出笑声。

branches.en: The skin carries the same touch inward as an itch.
branches.cn: 同样的轻触转到皮肤内部，就成了发痒。

branches.en: The laughter of sense one becomes a picture of being pleased.
branches.cn: 第一个义项里的笑，转化成了「被逗乐、被取悦」的画面。

branches.en: The light touch reaches the mind as interest and fancy.
branches.cn: 轻触延伸到心思上，就成了兴趣与喜好。

branches.en: The tingle itself, and the act that produces it, become a noun.
branches.cn: 那种刺痒感以及产生它的动作，都被名词化了。

intro.en: Tickle is a short native English verb; its word family is made with English suffixes such as -ish, -er, and -ing.
intro.cn: tickle 是简短的英语本土动词，词族由 -ish、-er、-ing 等英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The origin of tickle is uncertain and no reliable Latin source is known, so the Latin entries are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: tickle 的来源不确定，没有可靠的拉丁语来源，因此拉丁同源条留空。

items.meaning: to touch lightly so as to make someone laugh
items.example: Tickle is the base verb and noun.
items.exampleCN: tickle 是可作动词也可作名词的基础词。

items.example: Tikelen is the Middle English ancestor of tickle.
items.exampleCN: tikelen 是 tickle 的中古英语祖形。

items.example: The grass tickles my ankles.
items.exampleCN: 草蹭得我脚踝发痒。

items.meaning: past tense and past participle of tickle
items.meaningCN: tickle 的过去式和过去分词
items.example: She tickled the baby and he laughed.
items.exampleCN: 她挠了挠宝宝，宝宝笑了。

items.meaning: the act of tickling; also causing a tickle
items.meaningCN: 挠痒的动作；也指引起发痒的
items.example: He stopped tickling her when she said no.
items.exampleCN: 她说不要了，他就停止挠她。

items.example: The suffix -ish forms ticklish.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ish 构成 ticklish。

items.example: Ticklish describes sensitive skin and delicate matters.
items.exampleCN: ticklish 可以形容怕痒的皮肤，也可以形容敏感棘手的事。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 做某事的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms tickler.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 tickler。

items.meaning: a reminder note or memo book
items.example: He keeps a tickler file for weekly tasks.
items.exampleCN: 他用一个备忘夹记录每周要做的事。

definition_zh: 小口角；小争吵；轻微的不和；一时的怄气
definition_en: a small argument or petty quarrel, usually brief and not serious
core_image: 客厅中央两只杯子之间冒起的一小缕火星，亮一下就散了
scene: 恋爱节目里的两位嘉宾因为谁先挂断电话互相冷冷地顶了几句，旁边的朋友耸耸肩说这点小摩擦不算事。The presenter brushed off the sudden tiff between the two guests as nothing serious.
sceneCN: 这里 tiff 是「小口角」（第 1 个义项：两人之间短暂的小争吵）；句意：主持人把两位嘉宾之间突然的小口角当作没什么大不了的事。

derivatives.zh: 基础词 tiff 加进行词尾 -ing 构成，指拌嘴、小争执的行为或情形
基础词 tiff 加过去分词词尾构成，指拌过嘴、正怄着气的人

senses.title: A petty quarrel between two people
senses.definition: a brief argument over something small, especially between friends or partners
senses.definitionCN: 为小事发生的短暂争吵，尤其指朋友或伴侣之间
senses.example: The couple had a tiff over whose turn it was to cook.
senses.exampleCN: 这对情侣为轮到谁做饭拌了几句嘴。
senses.why: The word is recorded as a noun for petty anger in English well before its later senses, so a small quarrel is its oldest familiar use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词早在英语早期就作为名词指轻微的恼怒，所以「小争吵」是它最古老也最常用的用法。

senses.title: A fit of bad temper
senses.definition: a short spell of annoyance and sulking rather than a lasting feud
senses.definitionCN: 短暂的一阵恼火和闷气，而不是长期的仇怨
senses.example: She went quiet for an hour in a tiff and then started talking again.
senses.exampleCN: 她怄气沉默了一个小时，随后又开口说话了。
senses.why: Petty anger has to go somewhere, so the noun for a small quarrel also names the mood behind it.
senses.whyCN: 小小的恼怒总要有出口，于是表示小争吵的名词也用来指争吵背后的那股情绪。

senses.title: A slight clash of views
senses.definition: a minor disagreement between a team, a group, or public figures that does not break the relationship
senses.definitionCN: 团队、群体或公众人物之间并未破坏关系的轻微分歧
senses.example: A brief tiff over the budget was settled before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 关于预算的一次短暂意见不合在午饭前就解决了。
senses.why: When the quarrel is between groups rather than people, the word shifts from temper to a passing clash of opinion.
senses.whyCN: 当争吵发生在群体而非个人之间时，这个词就从情绪转向了一时的观点碰撞。

senses.title: To quarrel lightly
senses.definition: to argue with someone in a light, short way, often with a hint of affection
senses.definitionCN: 与某人轻松而简短地争几句，常带一点亲昵意味
senses.example: They tiff about housework almost every weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 他们几乎每个周末都为家务拌嘴。
senses.why: The noun was turned into a verb, so the same image of a short spark becomes an action.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词后来被用作动词，同一幅火花一闪的画面就变成了动作。

intro.en: Tiff has long been used for a small fit of temper or a petty quarrel, but its deeper origin is uncertain; a link to the verb meaning to sniff or puff is often suggested but not proved.
intro.cn: tiff 很久以来就用来指一阵小脾气或小争吵，但更深的来源不确定；常有人推测它与「喷鼻息、喘气」的古动词有关，不过并未得到证实。

items.en: The deeper source of the word is uncertain, and dictionaries mark it as of unknown origin.
items.cn: 这个词更深层的来源不确定，各词典都把它标为来源不明。

items.en: A verb tiff, meaning to sniff or puff, is recorded in the seventeen hundreds.
items.cn: 十七世纪记录了一个动词 tiff，意为喷鼻息、喘气。

items.en: The noun tiff, naming a fit of petty temper or a small quarrel, becomes common in the eighteen hundreds.
items.cn: 十八世纪，名词 tiff 指一阵小脾气或小争吵，变得常用起来。

items.en: Writers pair tiff with lovers and family members for everyday squabbles.
items.cn: 作家们把 tiff 用在情侣和家人身上，指日常的拌嘴。

items.en: Today tiff mainly names a brief, mild quarrel that soon blows over.
items.cn: 今天 tiff 主要指很快消散的短暂轻微争吵。

note.en: Tiff is close to quarrel and squabble in meaning, and to spit as a spelling look-alike, though the two spellings are unrelated.
note.cn: tiff 在意义上接近 quarrel 与 squabble，在拼写上又与 spit 相似，不过这两种拼写并无词源关系。

entries.definition: a light midday meal in India and Sri Lanka
entries.definitionCN: 印度和斯里兰卡的一顿简便午间餐；与 tiff 只是首字母相近，词源不同

entries.definition: hard and not easy to bend
entries.definitionCN: 僵硬、不容易弯曲的；与 tiff 在拼写上只差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: a drawer or machine that holds money in a shop
entries.definitionCN: 商店里放钱的抽屉或收银机；与 tiff 拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an angry argument between two people
entries.definitionCN: 两个人之间愤怒的争吵，比 tiff 更激烈，也常持续更久

entries.definition: a noisy argument about something unimportant
entries.definitionCN: 为小事吵闹的争执，往往杂乱而孩子气

entries.definition: a small, short quarrel
entries.definitionCN: 短暂的小争吵，含义与 tiff 非常接近

normalIntro.en: Tiff is a tiny, familiar word for a tiny, familiar quarrel, and its short shape matches the short length of such a row.
normalIntro.cn: tiff 是形容小小争吵的短小熟词，短短的形状正好对应这种争吵的短促。

normal.en: To have a tiff is to have a small quarrel that soon passes.
normal.cn: have a tiff 就是拌了一场很快过去的嘴。

normal.en: A lovers tiff is a petty row between partners.
normal.cn: lovers tiff 指伴侣之间的小吵小闹。

normal.en: A tiff is milder than a quarrel and shorter than a feud.
normal.cn: tiff 比 quarrel 温和，比 feud 短暂。

normal.en: The plural tiffs simply adds an s to the short form.
normal.cn: 复数 tiffs 只是在短词后加了一个 s。

normal.en: The verb use follows the noun, as in saying two friends tiff all afternoon.
normal.cn: 动词用法是从名词延伸来的，比如两位朋友拌了一下午嘴。

abstract.en: Picture two people turning away for a single minute and then turning back.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人扭过头去一小会儿，然后又转回来。

abstract.en: Imagine a lid lifted off a boiling pot just long enough for steam to hiss.
abstract.cn: 想象锅盖被掀起一小会儿，让蒸汽嘶嘶地冒出来。

abstract.en: See one red spot flashing twice on a screen and then going dark.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一颗红点亮了两下，随后暗了下去。

examples.en: The two flatmates had a tiff about the recycling and then went shopping together.
examples.cn: 两位室友为回收垃圾拌了几句嘴，然后还是一起去购物了。

examples.en: A trivial tiff between colleagues can echo through a whole office.
examples.cn: 同事之间一句小小的口角，也能在整间办公室里传开。

examples.en: He shrugged off the tiff with his brother as one of many.
examples.cn: 他把他和哥哥的口角看得稀松平常，说这只是许多次中的一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踢夫」——踢了丈夫一脚就拌起嘴来；只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：英语早期 tiff 先指一阵小脾气，后指小争吵；一般认为可能与指「喷鼻息」的古动词有关，但缺少可靠证据，属推测而非定论。

sensesIntro.en: Tiff moves from the brief quarrel itself, to the temper behind it, to a slight clash between groups, and finally to the light arguing action.
sensesIntro.cn: tiff 由争吵本身，延伸到争吵背后的情绪，再到群体之间的轻微碰撞，最后落到轻轻拌嘴的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small spark that flares between two people and dies down at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人之间冒出的一小簇火星，亮一下马上熄灭。

branches.en: The brief quarrel itself is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 短暂的口角本身是日常义项。

branches.en: The sulking mood is the sense of temper.
branches.cn: 闷闷不乐的情绪是情绪义项。

branches.en: A light clash of opinion is the group sense.
branches.cn: 轻微的意见碰撞是群体义项。

branches.en: A quarrel usually carries the bad temper with it.
branches.cn: 口角往往夹带着那股坏脾气。

branches.en: The noun and the verb name the same short, mild row.
branches.cn: 名词与动词指的是同一场短而温和的争吵。

intro.en: Tiff is a short, isolated word with no Latin ancestor, and English builds only a handful of forms around it, such as the plural tiffs and the rare verbal tiff.
intro.cn: tiff 是一个孤立的短词，没有拉丁语来源，英语围绕它构成的形态很少，例如复数 tiffs 和少见的动词 tiff。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word lies behind tiff, and its deeper origin remains uncertain, so the Latin family list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: tiff 背后没有拉丁语词，更深来源仍不确定，所以拉丁同族词列表为空。

items.example: The noun tiff is the whole word.
items.exampleCN: 名词 tiff 就是整个词的基本形式。

items.example: The plural tiffs adds a simple s.
items.exampleCN: 复数 tiffs 只加了一个 s。

items.example: The verb tiff reuses the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词 tiff 直接沿用名词。

items.example: The ending -ing forms tiffing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 tiffing。

items.example: The ending -ed forms tiffed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 tiffed。

items.meaning: to force liquid from the mouth
items.example: Spit looks close to tiff in print but is unrelated.
items.exampleCN: spit 印在纸上与 tiff 很像，但两者毫无关系。

items.example: Stiff adds one letter before tiff and shares no history.
items.exampleCN: stiff 在 tiff 前多一个字母，却没有共同历史。

items.example: Till keeps the first three letters of tiff.
items.exampleCN: till 保留了 tiff 的前三个字母。

items.example: Tiffin from South Asia only echoes the start of tiff.
items.exampleCN: 来自南亚的 tiffin 只是开头与 tiff 相似。

definition_zh: 拧紧；拉紧；收紧；加强（规定、管理）；变得更紧；变得紧张
definition_en: to make something closer, firmer, or stricter, or to become closer, firmer, or stricter
core_image: 一只手握住绳子末端，一圈一圈往回收，直到绳子一点空隙也不剩
scene: 车间里，一位修理工顺着螺栓的方向来回拧，直到扳手再也转不动为止。The mechanic used a long wrench to tighten the bolt on the machine.
sceneCN: 这里 tighten 是「拧紧」（第 1 个义项：把螺钉或绳扣收紧到不再松动）；句意：修理工用长扳手把机器上的螺栓拧紧。

pos.zh: 加强（规定、管理）；使更严格

derivatives.zh: 基础词 tighten 加名词词尾 -ing 构成，义为「紧缩、收紧」，如 tighten 与 -ing 组合出的 tightening of rules
基础词 tighten 加表示「工具、施动者」的词尾 -er 构成，指拧紧器、紧线器
形容词 tight 加名词词尾 -ness 构成，义为「紧密程度、绷紧状态」

senses.title: To make a screw, knot, or rope firm
senses.definition: to turn a screw or pull a rope until it is firm and cannot be moved further
senses.definitionCN: 转动螺钉或拉动绳子，直到它绷紧、再也动不了
senses.example: Please tighten the lid on the jar before you shake it.
senses.exampleCN: 摇晃罐子之前请先把盖子拧紧。
senses.why: The verb is simply the adjective tight plus the ending -en, which makes verbs, so it means to make something tight.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是形容词 tight 加上构成动词的词尾 -en，所以意思就是「使某物变紧」。

senses.title: To make a hold or grip stronger
senses.definition: to close your hand or arms more firmly around someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 用手或手臂更用力地围住某人或某物
senses.example: She tightened her grip on the handrail as the bus turned.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车转弯时，她把手扶杆握得更紧了。
senses.why: Hands are the first things people tighten, so the physical sense spreads to holding and gripping.
senses.whyCN: 手是最先被「收紧」的部位，于是物理意义自然扩展到握持与拥抱。

senses.title: To make rules or control stricter
senses.definition: to make laws, rules, or controls more strict and hard to avoid
senses.definitionCN: 使法律、规定或管制更严格、更难规避
senses.example: The airport tightened security after the alert.
senses.exampleCN: 预警发布后，机场加强了安保。
senses.why: A stricter rule is a tight rule, so making a rule stronger borrows the same tightening image.
senses.whyCN: 严格的规定就是「紧」的规定，所以让规定变得更严也借用了同一幅收紧的画面。

senses.title: To become tight or tense
senses.definition: to become firmer, tenser, or less relaxed without an outside actor
senses.definitionCN: 没有外力施动时，自己变得更紧、更绷、更不松弛
senses.example: Her shoulders tightened as she waited for the result.
senses.exampleCN: 等待结果时，她的肩膀绷紧了。
senses.why: The ending -en often marks both making and becoming, so tighten also stands alone as a change.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -en 常同时表示使动与自身变化，所以 tighten 也能单独表示「自己变得更紧」。

senses.title: To cut spending or supply
senses.definition: to reduce money, credit, or supplies so that less is available
senses.definitionCN: 削减资金、信贷或供应，使可用的更少
senses.example: The city had to tighten its budget after the floods.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，这座城市不得不紧缩预算。
senses.why: A tight budget leaves no slack, so to tighten a budget is to squeeze out free money.
senses.whyCN: 紧张的预算没有余量，所以紧缩预算就是把松动的钱挤掉。

intro.en: Tighten is an English formation: the adjective tight, which first described dense or firm things, took the verb ending -en, just as wide becomes widen and hard becomes harden.
intro.cn: tighten 是英语本土构成的词：形容词 tight 最初形容密实、牢固的东西，后来加上动词词尾 -en，就像 wide 变成 widen、hard 变成 harden。

items.en: A related Germanic form thykkr, meaning thick or close, lies behind the family.
items.cn: 同源的日耳曼语形式 thykkr 意为厚实、紧密，是这个词族的源头之一。

items.en: The adjective tight appears, meaning dense or firmly fixed.
items.cn: 形容词 tight 出现，意为密实或牢固固定。

items.en: Tight gains the sense of fitting closely and of being free of slack.
items.cn: tight 获得「贴身」和「没有松动余地」的含义。

items.en: The verb tighten is formed from tight with the ending -en.
items.cn: 动词 tighten 由 tight 加上词尾 -en 构成。

items.en: Tighten spreads from ropes and screws to rules, security, and budgets.
items.cn: tighten 从绳索、螺钉扩展到规定、安保与预算。

note.en: Tighten belongs to the tight family and contrasts with words of loosening, while its near meanings include tense, narrow, and stiffen.
note.cn: tighten 属于 tight 词族，与表示放松的词相对；近义场里还有 tense、narrow 与 stiffen。

entries.definition: firmly fixed, closely fitting, or strict
entries.definitionCN: 紧的；贴身的；严格的，是 tighten 的形容词原形

entries.definition: in a firm or close way
the state of being tight
to make procedures or systems stricter
to make something less firm or less tight
entries.definitionCN: 放松；松开，与 tighten 正好相反

entries.definition: stretched or firm from stress
to become or make firm and rigid

normalIntro.en: Tighten is tight plus the verb ending -en, so it names the act of turning something into a tight state.
normalIntro.cn: tighten 是 tight 加上动词词尾 -en，所以它指的是把某物变成「紧」的状态这个动作。

normal.en: To tighten something is to make it tight.
normal.cn: tighten 某物就是把它弄紧。

normal.en: The ending -en turns adjectives into verbs, as in widen and harden.
normal.cn: 词尾 -en 把形容词变成动词，widen 和 harden 都是这样。

normal.en: Tighten the screw means turn it until it stops.
normal.cn: tighten the screw 就是把螺钉拧到转不动为止。

normal.en: Tighten up often means make rules or checks stricter.
normal.cn: tighten up 常指把规定或检查做得更严。

normal.en: Its opposite is loosen, with the same -en ending.
normal.cn: 它的反义词是 loosen，同样带着 -en 词尾。

abstract.en: Picture one hand pulling a rope end by end.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手一点点地把绳子拉回。

abstract.en: Imagine teeth biting down on a zip as it is closed.
abstract.cn: 想象拉链拉起时，两排齿咬合到一起。

abstract.en: See a door with no gap left at the edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门关到边缘一点缝也不剩。

examples.en: The engineer tightened every bolt before the bridge reopened.
examples.cn: 桥梁重新开放之前，工程师把每一颗螺栓都拧紧了。

examples.en: Governments often tighten the rules after a serious accident.
examples.cn: 发生严重事故之后，政府常常会收紧相关规定。

examples.en: Her voice tightened when she heard the news.
examples.cn: 听到这个消息时，她的声音变得紧张起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太 tension」——紧到极限就是 tension，正好帮忙记住「拧紧、绷紧」的意思；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 古英语/中古英语 tight（密实、牢固，一般认为与古诺斯语 thykkr「厚实、紧密」同源）加动词化词尾 -en → tighten，核心义「使变紧」。

sensesIntro.en: Tighten first names the physical act of screwing or pulling, then a firmer hold, then stricter control, then a change that happens by itself, and finally the squeezing of money and supplies.
sensesIntro.cn: tighten 先指拧、拉的物理动作，再指更用力的握持，然后是更严的管制，接着是自身发生变化，最后是对钱与供应的紧缩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope pulled hand over hand until no slack remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：两手交替往回收绳，直到一点松量都不剩。

branches.en: Turning a screw or rope till it is firm is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 把螺钉或绳索转到绷紧是物理义项。

branches.en: A firmer grip is the body sense.
branches.cn: 更用力地握紧是身体义项。

branches.en: Stricter rules are the control sense.
branches.cn: 更严格的规定是管制义项。

branches.en: A body tensing and a budget shrinking both remove slack.
branches.cn: 身体绷紧与预算收缩都去掉了松动余地。

branches.en: Turning a screw and tightening rules share the same tightening image.
branches.cn: 拧螺钉与收紧规定共用同一幅收紧画面。

intro.en: Tighten is built from tight plus the Germanic ending -en, which forms verbs from adjectives, as in widen, harden, and darken.
intro.cn: tighten 由 tight 加日耳曼语词尾 -en 构成，这个词尾把形容词变成动词，例如 widen、harden、darken。

latinIntro.en: Tighten has no Latin ancestor; its core tight is Germanic, and Latin supplies only typological parallels such as the making verb endings.
latinIntro.cn: tighten 没有拉丁语来源，核心词 tight 属日耳曼语；拉丁语只提供可类比的构词方式，例如把形容词变成动词的附加手段。

items.example: Tight is the base adjective.
items.exampleCN: tight 是基础形容词。

items.example: The ending -en turns tight into tighten.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -en 把 tight 变成 tighten。

items.example: Tighten is the verb focus of this entry.
items.exampleCN: tighten 是这个词条的动词核心。

items.example: The ending -s forms tightens.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 tightens。

items.meaning: one that acts or a tool
items.example: The suffix -er gives tightener, a tool for tightening.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 tightener，指拧紧工具。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms tightly from tight.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 把 tight 变成 tightly。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms tightness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 tightness。

items.example: The ending -ing forms tightening as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成名词 tightening。

items.example: Loosen uses the same -en ending in the other direction.
items.exampleCN: loosen 用同一个 -en 词尾表示相反方向。

definition_zh: 可耕作的；适宜耕种的；可开垦为农田的
definition_en: suitable for being ploughed and used to grow crops
core_image: 一片松软的黑土，犁铧推过去，土块顺着犁沟翻滚成整齐的长条
scene: 一位农夫蹲在田边，捧起一把土在指间捻了捻，又看看坡度和石头多少，心里盘算这块地今年能种什么。The farmer tested the soil by hand to see whether the slope was tillable.
sceneCN: 这里 tillable 是「可耕作的」（第 1 个义项：土壤和地势适合翻耕种植）；句意：农夫用手检验土壤，想弄清这片坡地是否适合耕种。

pos.zh: 可耕作的；适宜耕种的；可开垦的

derivatives.zh: 基础词 tillable 去掉形容词词尾 -able 得到的动词原形，义为「耕作、翻地」
否定前缀 un- 加 tilled 构成，义为「未耕作的、荒着的」，与 tillable 描述的状态相关
动词 till 加名词词尾 -age 构成，义为「耕种、耕地作业」
动词 till 加表示施动者或工具的词尾 -er 构成，也可指农夫的耕地者或微耕机

senses.title: Suitable soil for ploughing and crops
senses.definition: describes soil or ground that can be ploughed and planted without serious difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 形容土壤或土地能够顺利翻耕、播种
senses.example: Only a narrow strip near the river is tillable.
senses.exampleCN: 只有靠近河边的一条狭长地带可以耕作。
senses.why: The verb till comes from Old English tilian, to work or cultivate, and -able adds can be done, giving can be tilled.
senses.whyCN: 动词 till 源自古英语 tilian（劳作、耕作），加上表示「可以被」的词尾 -able，就得到「可以被耕作」的意思。

senses.title: Land that can be brought under cultivation
senses.definition: describes land such as scrub, forest, or hillside that could be cleared and farmed
senses.definitionCN: 形容灌木地、林地或坡地中可以被清理出来用作农田的土地
senses.example: The plateau offers little tillable ground beyond the valley floor.
senses.exampleCN: 除了谷底，这片高原几乎没有什么可开垦的地。
senses.why: Once lands are studied for settlement, tillable moves from describing an existing field to estimating the future of uncultivated land.
senses.whyCN: 当人们研究定居选址时，tillable 就从描述现成的田地，扩展到估计未开垦土地的潜力。

senses.title: Ground that can be worked by machines
senses.definition: describes a plot whose size and shape allow ploughs, tractors, or seeders to work it
senses.definitionCN: 形容地块的大小与形状允许犁、拖拉机或播种机作业
senses.example: The small terraces are barely tillable with modern equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 这些小小的梯田几乎无法用现代设备耕作。
senses.why: Farming now means machines as much as hands, so a plot is tillable by machine as well as by anyone with a hoe.
senses.whyCN: 现代农业不仅靠手，也靠机械，所以一块地能否耕作，如今也看机器能否通行。

senses.title: Soil worth the work of farming
senses.definition: describes land whose crops would repay the cost of working it
senses.definitionCN: 形容耕作所得能够抵偿劳动成本的土地
senses.example: After erosion, the hillside was no longer tillable in any profitable way.
senses.exampleCN: 水土流失之后，那片山坡再怎么耕也赚不回成本了。
senses.why: Tilled land costs labour and money, so tillable also carries a quiet judgement about whether farming is worth it.
senses.whyCN: 耕地要花人力和本钱，因此 tillable 也暗含一层判断：这块地值不值得去耕。

intro.en: Tillable is an English formation from the verb till, which comes from Old English tilian, and the suffix -able, which marks what can be done.
intro.cn: tillable 是英语本土构成的词：由动词 till（源自古英语 tilian）加表示「可以被」的词尾 -able 组成。

items.en: Tilian means to strive for, work at, or cultivate.
items.cn: tilian 意为努力谋求、劳作或耕作。

items.en: Till, shortened from tilian, comes to mean to plough and raise crops.
items.cn: 由 tilian 缩短而来的 till，逐渐专指翻地、种庄稼。

items.en: The ending -able, borrowed through Old French from Latin -abilis, marks what can be done.
items.cn: 词尾 -able 经古法语借用自拉丁语 -abilis，表示「可以被……的」。

items.en: Tillage and tiller grow from till as farming language spreads.
items.cn: 随着农业用语普及，tillage 与 tiller 从 till 派生出来。

items.en: Tillable appears in land surveys, crop reports, and soil science writing.
items.cn: tillable 出现在土地调查、作物报告和土壤科学文献中。

note.en: Tillable shares its base with till, tillage, and tiller, and sits close to arable and cultivable in meaning.
note.cn: tillable 与 till、tillage、tiller 共用同一词基，在意义上与 arable、cultivable 很接近。

entries.definition: to prepare land by ploughing
entries.definitionCN: 翻地；耕作，是 tillable 的动词词基

entries.definition: the work of preparing land for crops
a person who tills, or a machine that breaks soil
never ploughed or left out of cultivation
suitable for growing crops, used mainly of farmland
entries.definitionCN: 可耕种的，多用于农田，与 tillable 含义最接近

entries.definition: able to be cultivated, used of land or of minds
entries.definitionCN: 可耕种的；可培育的，也能比喻才华

entries.definition: able to produce plenty of healthy crops
entries.definitionCN: 肥沃的，强调产量而不是能否翻耕

normalIntro.en: Tillable is till plus -able, so the whole word says that a piece of land can be tilled, and the longer forms tillage and tiller keep the same base.
normalIntro.cn: tillable 是 till 加 -able，整个词就是说一块地「可以被耕作」，而 tillage、tiller 也共享同一个词基。

normal.en: Tillable simply means able to be tilled.
normal.cn: tillable 的意思就是「可以被耕作」。

normal.en: The -able suffix marks what can be done, as in eatable and workable.
normal.cn: 词尾 -able 表示「可以……的」，eatable 与 workable 都是这样。

normal.en: Arable and tillable describe the same sort of land.
normal.cn: arable 与 tillable 描述的是同一类土地。

normal.en: Fields that are not worked are untilled, the opposite in practice.
normal.cn: 没有被耕作的地叫 untilled，实际效果正好相反。

normal.en: Tillable crops up in land surveys and farm reports.
normal.cn: tillable 常出现在土地调查和农场报告中。

abstract.en: Picture a plough turning soft dark earth into a neat furrow.
abstract.cn: 想象犁铧把深色的软土翻成一条整齐的犁沟。

abstract.en: Imagine a map with one green patch marked as good ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上有一小块绿色区域被标成好地。

abstract.en: See a tractor stopping at a fence because the next field is too rocky.
abstract.cn: 想象拖拉机在一块石头的田地前停下，因为那块地太硌了。

examples.en: The valley has rich tillable soil and reliable rain.
examples.cn: 这座山谷土壤肥沃，适宜耕种，雨水也十分可靠。

examples.en: Only a third of the island is tillable.
examples.cn: 这座岛上只有三分之一可以耕作。

examples.en: Engineers mapped the tillable area before the settlers arrived.
examples.cn: 在移民到来之前，工程师们测绘了可耕作区域。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提了把」锄头下地翻土——地能提得起犁、翻得动，就是「可耕作的」；只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 古英语 tilian（劳作；耕作）→ 英语 till（翻地、耕种）加拉丁—法语来源的形容词词尾 -able（可以被……的）→ tillable，核心义「能被翻耕种庄稼的」。

sensesIntro.en: Tillable starts with soil that can be ploughed, extends to land that could be opened up, then to ground machines can reach, and finally to land whose crops repay the effort.
sensesIntro.cn: tillable 先指能翻耕的土壤，再扩展到可开垦的土地，接着指机器能通行的地块，最后指耕作值得付出的土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plough blade slicing a neat furrow through soft dark earth.
core.cn: 核心意象：犁刃在松软的黑土中划出一条整齐的犁沟。

branches.en: Soil that can be ploughed is the core sense.
branches.cn: 能翻耕的土壤是核心义项。

branches.en: Land that could be opened up is the potential sense.
branches.cn: 可以被开垦的土地是潜力义项。

branches.en: Ground reachable by machines is the practical sense.
branches.cn: 机器能到达的地块是实用义项。

branches.en: Both fertile soil and machine access decide what one can farm.
branches.cn: 土壤肥力和机器通行共同决定能耕什么地。

branches.en: Fixing a price on new land links opening it up with its worth.
branches.cn: 为新地估量价值，把开垦潜力与经济收益连在一起。

intro.en: Tillable is till plus the adjective ending -able, and the till family runs through tillage, tiller, and untilled.
intro.cn: tillable 是 till 加形容词词尾 -able；till 词族还包括 tillage、tiller 与 untilled。

latinIntro.en: The base till is Germanic, but the ending -able came into English through Old French from Latin -abilis, the suffix of what can be done.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 till 属日耳曼语，但词尾 -able 经古法语来自拉丁语 -abilis，是表示「可以被……的」的形容词词尾。

items.example: Till is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: till 是这个词族的动词词基。

items.example: The ending -able turns till into tillable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 把 till 变成 tillable。

items.example: Tillable is the focus word of this entry.
items.exampleCN: tillable 是这个词条的核心词。

items.example: The ending -age gives tillage.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -age 构成 tillage。

items.meaning: one who acts or a tool
items.example: The ending -er gives tiller and a tiller machine.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 tiller，并可指耕地机。

items.example: The prefix un- gives untilled.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 untilled。

items.example: Latin -abilis is the ancestor of the ending -able.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -abilis 是词尾 -able 的祖先。

items.example: Arable uses the same ending as a near meaning.
items.exampleCN: arable 与近义词共用同一词尾。

items.example: Cultivable adds another -able word to the field.
items.exampleCN: cultivable 为这一义场再添一个 -able 词。

latinEntries.meaning: to till and improve the land

definition_zh: 倾斜；歪；使倾斜；倾斜面；倾向；偏向；抨击
definition_en: to move or cause to move into a sloping position, and the slope, leaning, or strong opinion that results from it
core_image: 桌面一角被垫高的书桌，桌面整个向一侧慢慢倒下
