scene: 桌子一条腿短了一截，桌面整个往一边歪。One leg of the table was short, so the top began to tilt towards the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 tilt 是「倾斜」（第 1 个义项：物体失去水平而歪向一边）；句意：桌子一条腿短了一截，桌面于是开始朝墙那边歪过去。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「倾斜的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「倾斜动作」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「使某物倾斜的人或装置」

senses.title: To lean or slope to one side
senses.definition: to move into a position that is not straight up and down or not level
senses.definitionCN: 移动成不再垂直或不再水平的位置
senses.example: The old bookshelf tilts slightly to the left.
senses.exampleCN: 那只旧书架稍稍往左歪。
senses.why: The oldest English tilt has the sense of being overturned or sloping, and a thing pushed off balance is the first picture the word draws.
senses.whyCN: 英语里 tilt 最早就表示被掀翻或歪斜，东西失去平衡的画面是这个词最先勾出的形象。

senses.title: To make something slope
senses.definition: to cause an object to move into a sloping position
senses.definitionCN: 使物体移到倾斜的位置
senses.example: He tilted the jug to pour out the last drops.
senses.exampleCN: 他把壶倾侧过来，倒出最后几滴。
senses.why: Once a thing can be slanted, a hand can do the slanting, so the verb gains a transitive sense.
senses.whyCN: 物体既然能歪，手就能把它歪过去，于是动词又多出及物的用法。

senses.title: A sloping position
senses.definition: an angle at which something is slanted
senses.definitionCN: 某物歪斜的角度
senses.example: The floor is built at a slight tilt so water runs away.
senses.exampleCN: 地面建得有轻微坡度，好让水流走。
senses.why: The action and the resulting angle are two faces of the same image, so a noun names the slant as a measured thing.
senses.whyCN: 动作和它留下的角度本是同一个意象的两面，名词因此把斜度当作一个可度量的结果来命名。

senses.title: A leaning of opinion
senses.definition: a tendency to favour one side in judgement or policy
senses.definitionCN: 判断或政策上偏向某一方的趋势
senses.example: The new policy has a leftward tilt on housing.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策在住房问题上带有左倾色彩。
senses.why: A surface that tilts sheds weight toward one side, and a mind that favours one side is pictured the same way.
senses.whyCN: 斜面会把分量卸向一边，心里偏向一方时也被画成同样的斜面。

senses.title: A jousting charge
senses.definition: a charge in which a rider thrusts a lance at an opponent
senses.definitionCN: 骑手举矛冲刺对手的比试动作
senses.example: The knights met in a tilt before the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士们在人群面前进行比武。
senses.why: In medieval times a tilt was a barrier between jousters and also the charge itself, an old sense that survives in literary use.
senses.whyCN: 在中世纪，tilt 既指比武场中的隔栏，也指那次冲锋，这个古老义项至今仍在文学里使用。

senses.title: To attack in words
senses.definition: to argue against or attack someone in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在言语或文字中攻击某人
senses.example: Critics tilt at the mayor over transport spending.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者们就交通开支抨击市长。
senses.why: The lance charge gives the fighting picture, so attacking with words borrows the same thrust.
senses.whyCN: 长矛冲锋提供了打斗画面，用言语攻击也就借用了同一股冲劲。

senses.title: At full speed
senses.definition: at maximum speed or effort, usually in the phrase full tilt
senses.definitionCN: 以最快速度或最大力气，常用于 full tilt 一词
senses.example: The children ran full tilt towards the swings.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们朝秋千全力跑去。
senses.why: A rider who charges at full tilt spurs his horse to its limit, and the phrase stretched to mean any rushing effort.
senses.whyCN: 骑士以全速冲锋时会策马到极限，这个短语后来被拉宽到指任何奋力冲刺。

intro.en: Tilt is recorded in Middle English as a verb meaning to overturn or fall over, and the noun seems to come from an older noun meaning a fall or a tumble.
intro.cn: tilt 在中古英语时期以动词形式出现，意为「翻倒、倒下」，名词则似乎来自更早一个意为「摔倒」的名词。

items.en: The verb tiltur appears with the sense of overturning or tumbling.
items.cn: 动词形式出现时带有「翻倒、摔倒」的意思。

items.en: The noun names a fall or an overthrow, and later a sloping position.
items.cn: 名词先指摔倒或倾覆，后来指倾斜的位置。

items.en: Tilt also names the barrier used in jousting and the charge itself.
items.cn: tilt 也指比武时用的隔栏以及那次冲锋。

items.en: The sense of a slope or slant widens to cover sloping ground and listing ships.
items.cn: 「斜面、歪斜」的意思扩大到坡地以及倾斜的船只。

items.en: Tilt gains figurative uses such as a lean in opinion and attacking in words.
items.cn: tilt 获得比喻用法，如观点的倾向和用言语攻击。

items.en: Mechanical uses spread to cameras, pinball tables, and tilt detectors.
items.cn: 机械用法扩展到相机、弹珠台和倾斜感应器。

note.en: Tilt neighbours slant, lean, and slope on the meaning side, and shares the spelling tip of tilt, title, and until on the form side.
note.cn: tilt 在意义上与 slant、lean、slope 相邻，在拼写上则与 tilt、title、until 共享同样的字母头尾。

entries.definition: stubble soil
entries.definitionCN: 此处仅作拼写对照：tilth 指耕过的表土，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: the name of a book or film
entries.definitionCN: 标题；书名，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: the handle of a sword
entries.definitionCN: 剑柄，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: to lean or slope to one side
to bend from an upright position
to be at an angle rather than flat

normalIntro.en: Tilt is a picture of balance lost: a surface that no longer stands level or straight.
normalIntro.cn: tilt 是一幅失去平衡的画面：表面不再水平，或者不再竖直。

normal.en: To tilt your head is to lean it to one side.
normal.cn: tilt your head 就是把头歪向一边。

normal.en: Something at a tilt is not straight.
normal.cn: at a tilt 表示处于歪斜状态。

normal.en: To tilt towards something is to lean in its direction, in body or in opinion.
normal.cn: tilt towards 就是身体或观点朝某方倾斜。

normal.en: To tilt at windmills comes from Don Quixote attacking imaginary foes.
normal.cn: tilt at windmills 出自堂吉诃德攻击假想敌人的故事。

normal.en: Full tilt means at top speed, as a knight charging at full gallop.
normal.cn: full tilt 意为全速，如同骑士催马全力冲锋。

abstract.en: Picture a table with one leg shorter than the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一张一条腿比别人短的桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a jug being tipped so the milk pours out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只壶被倾侧过来，牛奶倒了出来。

abstract.en: Picture a seesaw frozen at an angle halfway down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跷跷板停在半斜的角度上。

examples.en: She tilted her head to read the small print.
examples.cn: 她歪着头看小字。

examples.en: The ship began to tilt as the cargo shifted.
examples.cn: 货物滑移后，船开始倾斜。

examples.en: Supporters of the bill ran full tilt into the debate.
examples.cn: 法案的支持者全力投入这场辩论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踢了它」——一脚踢了桌腿，桌面就歪了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 tilt（翻倒、倾侧）→ 后起「倾斜；斜面」→ 比喻义「倾向、抨击」；另与中世纪比武的「长矛冲刺」同形并存，词根来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Tilt starts as a concrete slanting of an object, then names the angle itself, then a leaning of opinion, and finally the old jousting charge lends it senses of attack and full speed.
sensesIntro.cn: tilt 先是物体具体的歪斜，接着指歪出的角度，再用来指观点的倾斜，最后借古老的比武冲锋生出「抨击」和「全速」两个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table with one short leg, its top sliding into a slope.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条腿短了的桌子，桌面渐渐变成斜面。

branches.en: An object leaning off the vertical is the base sense.
branches.cn: 物体偏离竖直而歪斜是最基础的义项。

branches.en: The transitive version names the hand that does the tilting.
branches.cn: 及物用法指那只把东西倾侧过去的手。

branches.en: The slant frozen into a measured angle is the noun sense.
branches.cn: 把歪斜定格为一个可度量的角度，便是名词义项。

branches.en: Opinion can lean like a surface, giving the political sense.
branches.cn: 观点像表面一样可以倾斜，于是有了政治倾向义。

branches.en: The jousting charge branches out into verbal attack and full speed.
branches.cn: 比武冲锋这一支又分出言语攻击与全速两个义项。

intro.en: Tilt is a short native-looking word with few affixes, but it builds a family through tilt, tilted, tilting, and tilter.
intro.cn: tilt 是简短的本土面貌词，构词成分很少，却通过 tilted、tilting 与 tilter 形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Tilt is not Latin in origin and shares no Latin root, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: tilt 并非拉丁语来源，也没有拉丁词根，所以拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: Tilt carries the core picture of the sloping surface.
items.exampleCN: tilt 承载斜面这个核心画面。

items.example: The same spelling serves as the noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一拼写也用作名词。

items.meaningCN: 构成过去式或形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms tilted.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 tilted。

items.example: Tilted describes a surface that is not level.
items.exampleCN: tilted 描述不平的表面。

items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词或动作名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms tilting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 tilting。

items.example: Tilting names the motion itself.
items.exampleCN: tilting 指倾斜这个动作。

items.meaning: one who or that which does
items.meaningCN: 表示「做某事的人或物」的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms tilter.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 tilter。

items.meaning: a person or device that tilts
items.meaningCN: 使某物倾斜的人或装置
items.example: A tilter is rarely used outside machinery names.
items.exampleCN: tilter 除机械名称外很少使用。

items.example: Full tilt and at a tilt keep the noun sense.
items.exampleCN: full tilt 与 at a tilt 保留名词含义。

definition_zh: 音色；音质；音品
definition_en: the quality of a sound that lets you tell one voice or instrument from another
core_image: 同样敲一下，鼓是「咚」，钟是「铛」，木头是「笃」——形状不同，颜色就不同
scene: 同一首曲子，长笛和提琴各奏一遍，立刻听出不同。The flute and the violin play the same tune, and their different timbre makes each instantly recognisable.
sceneCN: 这里 timbre 是「音色」（第 1 个义项：声音的独特质量）；句意：长笛和小提琴演奏同一首曲子，两者不同的音色让人一听就能分辨。

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -al 构成，义为「音色的」
由名词加 -less 构成，义为「没有音色的」

senses.title: The colour of a sound
senses.definition: the distinctive quality that makes one sound or voice different from another of the same pitch and loudness
senses.definitionCN: 在同音高、同响度下使一种声音区别于另一种声音的独特品质
senses.example: Each singer in the choir has a different timbre.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团里每位歌手都有不同的音色。
senses.why: The French word carried the picture of a bell struck and sounding, and that struck quality is exactly what listeners call the colour of a sound.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语词从前带着「钟被敲响」的画面，而钟被敲出的那种质地，正是听者所说的声音的颜色。

senses.title: A characteristic voice quality
senses.definition: the personal tone that lets you recognise a particular speaker
senses.definitionCN: 能让人认出某个说话者的个人嗓音特征
senses.example: I knew her voice at once from its soft timbre.
senses.exampleCN: 凭那柔和的音色，我一下就听出是她的声音。
senses.why: A voice is a living instrument, so the same musical colour can mark a person like a fingerprint.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音就像一件活的乐器，同一种音乐上的色彩因此能像指纹一样标记一个人。

senses.title: The character of a place or writing
senses.definition: the general feeling or flavour of a place, text, or period
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方、文字或时代给人的总体感觉或味道
senses.example: The essay has the timbre of a winter letter.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章带着冬日书信的情调。
senses.why: From it, though his rest is deep, the sound of what he was still steals, and so timbre stretches from sound to the overall note of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 按原句大意：人虽沉睡，旧日模样仍悄然作响，于是 timbre 从声音延伸到事物的整体调子。

intro.en: Timbre comes from French timbre, which first meant a small bell or the stamp of a bell, and the modern musical sense was taken up in French before reaching English.
intro.cn: timbre 来自法语 timbre，原本指小钟或钟的印记，现代的「音色」义先由法语采用，再进入英语。

items.en: Tympanon names a drum made of a stretched skin.
items.cn: tympanon 指蒙皮制成的鼓。

items.en: Tympanum keeps the sense of a drum or a timbrel.
items.cn: tympanum 保留鼓或手鼓的意思。

items.en: Timbre names a small bell and also the stamp that a herald uses on a shield.
items.cn: timbre 指小钟，也指纹章官盖在盾牌上的印记。

items.en: French musicians apply timbre to the colour of an instrument or voice.
items.cn: 法语音乐家把 timbre 用来指乐器或人声的音色。

items.en: English adopts timbre for the quality of a musical sound.
items.cn: 英语借用 timbre，指乐音的品质。

items.en: Timbre spreads to voice, speech, and even literary tone.
items.cn: timbre 扩展到人声、言语甚至文学调子。

note.en: Timbre is a technical word in the field of sound, close to tone and resonance on the meaning side and to timber on the spelling side.
note.cn: timbre 是声音领域的专业词，意义上接近 tone 与 resonance，拼写上也容易和 timber 混淆。

entries.definition: wood prepared for building
entries.definitionCN: 木材；木料，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: a small hand drum
entries.definitionCN: 小铃鼓，与 timbre 共享「敲击发声」的古远来源。

entries.definition: a drum or a sounding membrane
entries.definitionCN: 鼓；鼓膜，经由拉丁语与 timbre 同源，只是拼写不同。

entries.definition: the quality of a sound
the deep full quality of a sound
how high or low a sound is

normalIntro.en: Timbre is the colour of sound: the same note sounds different on a drum, a bell, and a flute.
normalIntro.cn: timbre 是声音的颜色：同一个音，打在鼓上、钟上和长笛上听起来完全不同。

normal.en: A rich timbre suggests a warm, full instrument.
normal.cn: rich timbre 暗示乐器温暖而饱满。

normal.en: A distinctive timbre makes a singer easy to recognise.
normal.cn: distinctive timbre 让歌手容易被辨认。

normal.en: The timbre of a voice is like its fingerprint.
normal.cn: the timbre of a voice 就像声音的指纹。

normal.en: Keep timber in mind as a false friend: timber is wood, timbre is sound.
normal.cn: 记住 timber 是假朋友：timber 是木头，timbre 是声音。

normal.en: The old French sense of a struck bell explains why timbre describes how a sound is made.
normal.cn: 古法语里「敲响的钟」这一义，解释了为什么 timbre 描述声音是怎么出来的。

abstract.en: Picture one note on three instruments: drum, bell, flute.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个音在鼓、钟、长笛上各敲一次。

abstract.en: Picture light passing through coloured glass: same light, different colour.
abstract.cn: 想象光线穿过不同颜色的玻璃：同一种光，颜色却不同。

abstract.en: Picture a deep bell sound fading in a cold night air.
abstract.cn: 想象一声深沉的钟音在寒夜里慢慢散去。

examples.en: The cello has a deep, warm timbre.
examples.cn: 大提琴的音色深沉而温暖。

examples.en: Her timbre was so clear that I knew the caller at once.
examples.cn: 她的音色那么清楚，我一下子就知道了来电的是谁。

examples.en: Modern recordings preserve the original timbre of old instruments.
examples.cn: 现代录音保留了老乐器的原有音色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「听吧」——竖耳一听，就能分辨乐器的音色；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古希腊语 tympanon（鼓）→ 拉丁语 tympanum（鼓）→ 古法语 timbre（小钟；印记）→ 法语音乐术语 timbre（音色）→ 英语 timbre，核心义「敲响之物发出的独特声音」。

sensesIntro.en: Timbre first names the colour of a musical sound, then the personal quality of a voice, and finally the general tone or flavour of a place or a piece of writing.
sensesIntro.cn: timbre 先指乐音的音色，再指人声的个人特质，最后扩大到某个地方或一篇文章的整体调子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same note rung on a drum, a bell, and a flute.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个音分别在鼓、钟和长笛上响起。

branches.en: The struck-bell picture becomes the colour of a musical sound.
branches.cn: 敲钟的画面转化为乐音的色彩，即第 1 个义项。

branches.en: A voice is the everyday instrument, so timbre marks a speaker.
branches.cn: 人声是日常的乐器，所以 timbre 标记说话的人。

branches.en: The sound-metaphor stretches to places, texts, and periods.
branches.cn: 声音的比喻扩展到地方、文字与时代。

branches.en: Both musical instruments and human voices have a recognisable colour.
branches.cn: 乐器和人声都带有可辨认的色彩。

branches.en: A voice and a piece of writing can share the same soft or sharp tone.
branches.cn: 一个声音和一篇文章可以拥有同样柔和或尖锐的调子。

intro.en: Timbre is a loanword from French, so its affixes are mostly derived forms such as timbral and timbreless.
intro.cn: timbre 是从法语借来的外来词，英语中相关派生主要靠 timbral 与 timbreless 这类后缀形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin tympanum, from Greek tympanon, means a drum, and it is the distant source behind timbre.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tympanum 源于希腊语 tympanon，意为「鼓」，是 timbre 遥远的前身。

items.example: Timbre keeps the French spelling.
items.exampleCN: timbre 保留法语的拼写。

items.example: The suffix -al forms timbral.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 timbral。

items.example: Timbral changes are easy to hear.
items.exampleCN: 音色的变化很容易听出来。

items.example: The suffix -less forms timbreless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 timbreless。

items.example: Timbreless describes a flat sound.
items.exampleCN: timbreless 描述平淡的声音。

items.example: The suffix -s forms timbres.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 timbres。

items.example: Timbres vary between instruments.
items.exampleCN: 各乐器的音色各不相同。

items.example: Rich timbre and warm timbre are common descriptions.
items.exampleCN: rich timbre 与 warm timbre 是常见的描述。

definition_zh: 胆小的；羞怯的；畏缩的；缺乏自信的
definition_en: easily frightened and not confident, especially in the face of new people or situations
core_image: 门口站着的孩子，手一直摸着门框，脚尖反复在地上蹭，不敢迈进去
scene: 新来的同学站在教室门口，半天不敢进去打招呼。The new pupil was too timid to walk into the classroom and say hello.
sceneCN: 这里 timid 是「羞怯的」（第 1 个义项：面对生人不敢上前）；句意：这个新同学太胆小了，不敢走进教室打招呼。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ity 构成，义为「胆怯；羞怯」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「胆怯地」
来自拉丁语，与 timid 同源，义为「恐吓；威胁」
intimidate 的名词形式，义为「恐吓、胁迫」

senses.title: Easily frightened of people
senses.definition: nervous and shy when meeting other people or speaking in public
senses.definitionCN: 见到别人或在众人面前说话时紧张害羞
senses.example: The timid boy hid behind his mother.
senses.exampleCN: 那个怕生的男孩躲到母亲身后。
senses.why: The Latin source means full of fear, and the first place fear shows is in the company of others.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「充满恐惧」，恐惧最先出现的地方往往就是在人前。

senses.title: Lacking boldness
senses.definition: not brave enough to take risks or act boldly
senses.definitionCN: 胆子不够大，不敢冒险或大胆行动
senses.example: The company made a timid move into the new market.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司进入新市场时小心翼翼。
senses.why: From fearing people it is a short step to fearing action, so timid shades into a lack of boldness in decisions.
senses.whyCN: 从怕人只需一小步就走到怕行动，于是 timid 也带上决策上不够果敢的意思。

senses.title: Faint and hesitant
senses.definition: expressed weakly or without confidence
senses.definitionCN: 表达得微弱而缺乏信心
senses.example: She gave a timid knock at the heavy door.
senses.exampleCN: 她在厚重的门上怯生生地敲了一下。
senses.why: Fear shrinks the movements that express it, so a timid knock or voice is small and hesitant.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧让表达它的动作变得很小，所以 timid 的敲门声或声音是微弱而迟疑的。

intro.en: Timid comes from Latin timidus, meaning fearful, from the verb timere, to fear, and it entered English through French
intro.cn: timid 来自拉丁语 timidus（害怕的），源于动词 timere（害怕），并经由法语进入英语

items.en: Timere means to fear or dread, and timidus means full of fear.
items.cn: timere 意为害怕、惧怕，timidus 意为充满恐惧的。

items.en: Timidus describes a person who shrinks from danger or from strangers.
items.cn: timidus 描述见到危险或生人便退缩的人。

items.en: The adjective enters French as timide with the same fearful sense.
items.cn: 这个形容词以 timide 进入法语，意思同样是胆怯的。

items.en: English borrows it and applies it to a shy person.
items.cn: 英语把它借来，用于形容羞怯的人。

items.en: The word stretches to weak or cautious actions, such as a timid question.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到微弱或谨慎的行动，例如怯生生的问题。

items.en: The family around timere grows with intimidate and intimidation.
items.cn: 围绕 timere 的词族随 intimidate 与 intimidation 一起扩展。

note.en: Timid joins the family of timere, fear, and stands near shy, bashful, and hesitant in the field of feeling.
note.cn: timid 属于 timere（害怕）这一词族，在情感义场里与 shy、bashful、hesitant 相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being timid
in a shy or fearful manner
easily frightened
entries.definitionCN: 胆怯的，与 timid 同根，来自拉丁语 timor（恐惧）。

entries.definition: to frighten someone into doing something
nervous around other people
easily embarrassed and shy
slow to act or speak because of doubt

normalIntro.en: Timid is fear made small: the person who wants to step forward takes half a step back.
normalIntro.cn: timid 是被缩小的恐惧：想往前迈步的人，反而退了半步。

normal.en: A timid child often hides behind a parent.
normal.cn: 胆小的孩子常躲在父母身后。

normal.en: A timid smile is small and unsure.
normal.cn: a timid smile 是微小而不确定的微笑。

normal.en: Too timid to speak, she stayed silent all evening.
normal.cn: 胆小得不敢开口，她整晚都没说话。

normal.en: The noun timidity adds -ity, and the adverb timidly adds -ly.
normal.cn: 名词 timidity 加 -ity，副词 timidly 加 -ly。

normal.en: Intimidate is the same root with in-, to put fear into someone.
normal.cn: intimidate 是同一词根加 in-，意为把恐惧放进别人心里。

abstract.en: Picture a child gripping the door frame before a school entrance.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子在学校门口紧抓门框。

abstract.en: Picture a small candle flame that a breath could put out.
abstract.cn: 想象一簇小烛火，一口气就能吹灭。

abstract.en: Picture a tortoise retracting its head at a footstep.
abstract.cn: 想象一只乌龟听到脚步声就缩回脑袋。

examples.en: The timid puppy stayed under the chair for an hour.
examples.cn: 那只胆小的小狗在椅子下待了一个钟头。

examples.en: He was too timid to ask for a raise.
examples.cn: 他太胆小，不敢要求加薪。

examples.en: Her timid reply showed that she did not trust the plan.
examples.cn: 她怯生生的回答说明她并不信任这个计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踢米的小人」——一个连踢米都怕的小矮人，胆子太小；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 timere（害怕）→ timidus（害怕的）→ 中古法语 timide → 英语 timid，核心义「心里装满恐惧」。

sensesIntro.en: Timid starts as fear of other people, then fear of acting boldly, and finally fear made visible in small, hesitant sounds and gestures.
sensesIntro.cn: timid 先是怕人，接着是怕大胆行动，最后指以怯生生的小动作和声音表现出来的那份恐惧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child gripping the door frame, afraid to step inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个孩子抓着门框，不敢迈进门里。

branches.en: The plain fear of people is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 直接怕人是这个字最日常的义项。

branches.en: Fear spreading to decisions gives the sense of lacking boldness.
branches.cn: 恐惧蔓延到决策，便生出了缺乏胆量的义项。

branches.en: Fear shown as small gestures is the faint, hesitant sense.
branches.cn: 以小动作表现出的恐惧就是怯生生、微弱的义项。

branches.en: A shy person and a cautious plan both shrink from risk.
branches.cn: 羞怯的人和谨慎的方案都在风险面前退缩。

branches.en: A timid move is both unambitious and weakly expressed.
branches.cn: 怯生生的举动既不敢下重手，也表现得微弱。

intro.en: Timid builds a family with the Latin root tim-, seen in timidity and intimidating, plus the hidden in- in intimidate.
intro.cn: timid 靠拉丁词根 tim- 组成词族，见于 timidity 与 intimidating，而 intimidate 里还藏着一个 in-。

latinIntro.en: Latin timere means to fear, and timidus means fearful, while tremere, to tremble, is often linked to it through an uncertain consonant change.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 timere 意为害怕，timidus 意为胆怯的；tremere（发抖）常被认为与它有关，但辅音变化是否成立来源不确定。

items.example: The root tim- carries the nervous shiver.
items.exampleCN: 词根 tim- 带着那种紧张的颤意。

items.example: Timid comes through French.
items.exampleCN: timid 经由法语而来。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms timidity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 timidity。

items.example: Timidity describes the state.
items.exampleCN: timidity 描述这种状态。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms timidly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 timidly。

items.example: She spoke timidly.
items.exampleCN: 她怯生生地说话。

items.example: The prefix in- appears in intimidate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 出现在 intimidate 中。

items.example: Intimidate means to put fear into someone.
items.exampleCN: intimidate 意为把恐惧注入别人心里。

items.example: Timorous is a literary cousin of timid.
items.exampleCN: timorous 是 timid 在文学里的近亲。

definition_zh: 胆怯；羞怯；畏缩；缺乏勇气
definition_en: the quality of being shy, nervous, and easily frightened, especially in front of other people
core_image: 一只小鹿在林边停下脚步，听到动静就缩回树后
scene: 轮到他在会上发言时，他低着头、声音发颤，一句话也没能说完整。His timidity kept him silent whenever the teacher asked a question.
sceneCN: 这里 timidity 是「胆怯、羞怯」（第 1 个义项：性格上的害羞与缺乏勇气）；句意：每当老师提问，他的胆怯总让他沉默不语。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「胆小的；羞怯的」，timidity 由它加名词后缀 -ity 构成
基础形容词 timid 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「怯生生地；畏缩地」
拉丁前缀 in-（使进入）+ timidus 构成，义为「吓唬；威胁」，与 timid 同源
intimidate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「恐吓；胁迫」

senses.title: Shyness that holds a person back
senses.definition: the habit of feeling shy and afraid to speak or act in front of others
senses.definitionCN: 在他人面前害羞、不敢说话或行动的性情
senses.example: Her timidity made her avoid the school debate team.
senses.exampleCN: 她的胆怯让她躲开了校辩论队。
senses.why: The core image is a creature that shrinks back, so the abstract noun names the habit of shrinking from people.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是遇人即退缩的小动物，因此这个抽象名词指「面对他人就退缩」的习性。

senses.title: Nervousness in a new situation
senses.definition: a nervous, hesitant feeling in an unfamiliar place or when meeting strangers
senses.definitionCN: 在陌生环境或初见生人时紧张、犹豫不安的感觉
senses.example: New students often show timidity on their first day.
senses.exampleCN: 新生在第一天常显出胆怯。
senses.why: The same shrinking reflex appears in any situation that feels new, so the noun also names situational nervousness.
senses.whyCN: 同样的退缩本能在任何陌生情境中都会出现，所以这个词也指特定场合下的紧张不安。

senses.title: Lack of boldness in a decision
senses.definition: a lack of courage or boldness when a firm move is needed
senses.definitionCN: 在需要果断行动时缺乏勇气或魄力
senses.example: The committee was criticised for its timidity in reform.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会因改革中畏手畏脚而受到批评。
senses.why: If a person never steps forward, the shrinking becomes a trait of choices, so the noun can criticise weak action.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人始终不敢迈步，退缩就成了行动的特点，于是这个词也可用来批评行动不够果断。

intro.en: Timidity comes from Latin timidus, fearful, from timere, to fear, and reached English through French before the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: timidity 来自拉丁语 timidus（害怕的），源于 timere（恐惧），十六世纪前经由法语进入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root behind timere is usually connected with the idea of fear or dread.
items.cn: 一般认为，timere 背后的重构词根与恐惧、惊慌有关。

items.en: Timere means to be afraid, and timidus means fearful.
items.cn: timere 意为害怕，timidus 意为胆小的。

items.en: Timiditas is formed with the abstract noun suffix -itas.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用抽象名词后缀 -itas 构成 timiditas。

items.en: French carries the adjective timide and the abstract noun timidite.
items.cn: 法语带来形容词 timide 与抽象名词 timidite。

items.en: English timidity settles the -ity spelling and now also criticises weak policy.
items.cn: 英语 timidity 固定了 -ity 拼写，如今还用来批评政策上的畏缩。

note.en: Timidity belongs to the timid family of fear words and sits beside shyness and cowardice in meaning.
note.cn: timidity 属于以 timid 为核心的「恐惧」词族，在意义上与羞怯、懦弱相邻。

entries.definition: shy and easily frightened
in a shy and fearful way
to frighten someone into doing or not doing something
an uncomfortable feeling when meeting other people
the lack of courage to face danger or pain
the act of pausing before acting

normalIntro.en: Timidity is the state of being timid: a small animal that keeps its head down.
normalIntro.cn: timidity 就是 timid 的状态名词：像一只总低着头的幼小动物。

normal.en: Timidity = timid + -ity, the noun ending for a quality.
normal.cn: timidity 等于 timid 加 -ity，-ity 是表示性质的名词后缀。

normal.en: To shake off timidity is to stop hiding behind others.
normal.cn: shake off timidity 就是不再躲在别人身后。

normal.en: Timid speaks quietly; timidity is the quietness itself.
normal.cn: timid 是轻声说话的样子，timidity 则是那份安静本身。

normal.en: Intimidate adds in-, to put fear into someone, and shares the root tim-.
normal.cn: intimidate 加上 in-，意思是把恐惧放进别人心里，共享 tim- 词根。

normal.en: Compare shyness: shyness is social, timidity spreads to all that frightens.
normal.cn: 对比 shyness：羞怯偏社交场合，timidity 则涵盖一切令人害怕的事。

abstract.en: Picture a deer that stops mid-step and slips back behind a tree.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小鹿走到一半停住，退回树后。

abstract.en: Imagine a student who knows the answer but hides in the last row.
abstract.cn: 想象一个知道答案却躲到最后一排的学生。

abstract.en: Think of a driver who stays stuck at the junction for a minute.
abstract.cn: 想象一位司机在路口停了一分钟不敢通过。

examples.en: He overcame his timidity and asked her to dance.
examples.cn: 他克服了胆怯，请她跳舞。

examples.en: The team lost because of its timidity in the final minutes.
examples.cn: 这个队因为最后几分钟的畏缩而输了比赛。

examples.en: Her timidity vanished once she was on stage.
examples.cn: 她一上台，胆怯就消失了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「替他 -> 替…回避」——总想替自己躲开人群，就是胆怯；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 timere（害怕）→ timidus（胆小的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 timiditas（胆怯）→ 古法语 timidite → 英语 timidity，核心义「遇事就退缩的害怕」。

sensesIntro.en: Timidity starts as a personal shyness, widens to nervousness in new places, and can finally describe weak, fearful decisions.
sensesIntro.cn: timidity 先指个人性格上的羞怯，再扩展为陌生场合的紧张，最后可指决策上的畏缩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small deer that stops and slips back behind a tree.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小鹿停下脚步，缩回到树后。

branches.en: Personal shyness is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 性格上的羞怯是日常义项。

branches.en: Nervousness in new places is the situational sense.
branches.cn: 陌生场合的紧张是情境义项。

branches.en: Lack of boldness is the critical sense.
branches.cn: 缺乏魄力是带有批评意味的义项。

branches.en: Both shyness and first-day nerves make a person look quieter than usual.
branches.cn: 羞怯与第一天的紧张都会让人显得比平常更沉默。

branches.en: A hesitant newcomer and a timid committee both avoid the forward step.
branches.cn: 犹豫的新来者与畏缩的委员会都不肯迈出那一步。

intro.en: Timidity pairs the fear root tim- with the Latin abstract suffix -ity, and grows a family of timid, timidly, and intimidate.
intro.cn: timidity 把表示恐惧的词根 tim- 与拉丁抽象名词后缀 -ity 结合，并衍生出 timid、timidly、intimidate 等同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin timere means to fear; timidus is fearful, and timiditas is the abstract fearfulness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 timere 意为害怕，timidus 意为胆小的，timiditas 意为胆怯这一抽象性质。

items.example: The root tim- carries the idea of fear in the family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 tim- 在这个词族中承载「恐惧」之意。

items.example: Timere is the source verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: timere 是这个词族的源头动词。

items.example: Timidus gives English timid.
items.exampleCN: timidus 演变出英语 timid。

items.example: Timid is the base adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: timid 是词族的基础形容词。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The Latin suffix -ity turns timid into timidity.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁后缀 -ity 把 timid 变成 timidity。

items.meaningCN: 表示方式或样子的副词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ly turns timid into timidly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把 timid 变成 timidly。

items.example: Timidly describes a shrinking manner.
items.exampleCN: timidly 描述畏缩的方式。

items.example: The prefix in- combines with timid to form intimidate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 与 timid 结合构成 intimidate。

items.meaning: to frighten into action or silence
items.example: Intimidate means to put fear into someone.
items.exampleCN: intimidate 意为把恐惧注入他人心中。

items.example: The verb suffix -ate helps form intimidate.
items.exampleCN: 动词后缀 -ate 参与构成 intimidate。

definition_zh: 胆怯地；羞怯地；畏畏缩缩地
definition_en: in a shy, nervous, and easily frightened way
core_image: 一只手推开门缝，只探出半个脑袋往里偷看
scene: 门外的少年抬手敲了两下，又急忙把手缩回来，眼睛盯着自己的鞋尖。She knocked timidly and lowered her eyes as soon as the door opened.
sceneCN: 这里 timidly 是「怯生生地」（第 1 个义项：说话或行动时带着害羞与害怕的样子）；句意：她怯怯地敲了敲门，门一开就垂下了眼睛。

pos.zh: 胆怯地；羞怯地；畏畏缩缩地

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「胆小的；羞怯的」，timidly 由它加 -ly 构成
基础形容词 timid 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「胆怯；羞怯」
拉丁前缀 in-（使进入）+ timidus 构成，义为「恐吓；威胁」

senses.title: In a shy and nervous way
senses.definition: in a manner that shows shyness and fear of other people
senses.definitionCN: 以显出羞怯、害怕他人的方式
senses.example: The boy answered timidly, hardly raising his head.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩几乎不抬头，怯生生地回答。
senses.why: The adverb copies the shrinking picture of timid and attaches it to the way an action is done.
senses.whyCN: 副词把 timid 那种「缩回去」的画面，附加在动作进行的方式上。

senses.title: With hesitant, small steps
senses.definition: in a hesitant way, as if unsure whether to go on
senses.definitionCN: 以犹豫不决、好像不确定是否该继续的方式
senses.example: He stepped timidly into the empty hall.
senses.exampleCN: 他畏畏缩缩地走进了空荡的大厅。
senses.why: A fearful creature moves in short, uncertain steps, so the adverb also marks hesitating movement.
senses.whyCN: 害怕的动物总是一小步一小步地试探，所以这个副词也标记犹豫的动作。

senses.title: With a quiet, weak manner
senses.definition: in a low, weak manner that suggests little confidence
senses.definitionCN: 以声音低、底气不足、显得不太自信的方式
senses.example: She smiled timidly and said nothing more.
senses.exampleCN: 她浅浅地笑了笑，没再多说什么。
senses.why: When courage falls, the voice and gesture shrink too, so the adverb can describe a faint, guarded manner.
senses.whyCN: 勇气一减，声音和动作也跟着变小，于是这个副词也能形容轻而拘谨的样子。

intro.en: Timidly is the adverb of timid, from Latin timidus, fearful, and timere, to fear, with the English adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: timidly 是 timid 的副词形式，源自拉丁语 timidus（害怕的）与 timere（恐惧），并加上英语副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Timere means to be afraid, and timidus means fearful.
items.cn: timere 意为害怕，timidus 意为胆小的。

items.en: French timide means shy or fearful and carries the word root north.
items.cn: 法语 timide 意为羞怯或害怕，把词根带入北方。

items.en: English borrows the adjective timid, meaning fearful.
items.cn: 英语借入形容词 timid，表示害怕的。

items.en: The suffix -ly attaches to timid to make the adverb timidly.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 附加在 timid 上，构成副词 timidly。

items.en: Timidly now mainly describes shy, nervous behaviour rather than open danger.
items.cn: 现代英语中 timidly 主要描写羞怯紧张的举止，而非面对真实危险。

note.en: Timidly is the adverb of the timid family and closely matches shyly, nervously, and hesitantly in meaning.
note.cn: timidly 是以 timid 为核心词族的副词，意义上与 shyly、nervously、hesitantly 相近。

the quality of being shy and fearful
to frighten someone into doing something
in a way that shows discomfort with other people
