normalIntro.en: Timidly says how a timid person acts: quietly, carefully, with eyes down.
normalIntro.cn: timidly 说明一个胆怯的人如何行动：轻声、小心、低着头。

normal.en: Timidly = timid + -ly, so it keeps the shy adjective whole.
normal.cn: timidly 等于 timid 加 -ly，完整保留了「羞怯」这个形容词。

normal.en: To ask timidly is to ask with your voice almost disappearing.
normal.cn: ask timidly 就是声音几乎要消失地问。

normal.en: Adverbs end in -ly, so timidly describes the how of an action.
normal.cn: 副词多以后缀 -ly 结尾，因此 timidly 描述动作是怎样进行的。

normal.en: Timidity is the feeling; timidly is the walk that feeling produces.
normal.cn: timidity 是那种感觉，timidly 则是那种感觉带来的走姿。

normal.en: Compare boldly: boldly steps forward, timidly steps back.
normal.cn: 对比 boldly：大胆是向前一步，胆怯是向后一缩。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that pushes a door open only halfway.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手只把门推开一半。

abstract.en: Imagine a half-head peeping round a door frame.
abstract.cn: 想象半个脑袋从门框边探出来偷看。

abstract.en: Think of a smile that appears and disappears in a second.
abstract.cn: 想象一个一闪就收回去的微笑。

examples.en: The girl raised her hand timidly in class.
examples.cn: 女孩在课堂上怯生生地举起了手。

examples.en: He walked timidly down the corridor, listening for every sound.
examples.cn: 他怯怯地走过走廊，留意着每一个声响。

examples.en: She asked timidly whether she could sit beside us.
examples.cn: 她怯怯地问能不能坐在我们旁边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踢米地」——像小猫踢着米粒、贴着地面小步挪动，一副不敢声张的样子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 timere（害怕）→ timidus（胆小的）→ 古法语 timide → 英语 timid（胆小的）→ 加 -ly 构成副词 timidly，核心义「以畏缩的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Timidly first describes shy speech, then hesitant movement, and finally a faint, guarded manner.
sensesIntro.cn: timidly 先形容羞怯的说话，再形容犹豫的动作，最后形容轻而拘谨的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a door open only halfway.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手只把门推开一半。

branches.en: Shy speech is the main adverbial sense.
branches.cn: 羞怯地说话是主要的副词义项。

branches.en: Hesitant movement is the motion sense.
branches.cn: 犹豫的动作是运动类义项。

branches.en: A faint manner is the tone sense.
branches.cn: 轻而拘谨的样子是语气类义项。

branches.en: A timidly asked question and a timidly taken step share the same shrinking body.
branches.cn: 怯怯地问出的问题和怯怯迈出的一步，来自同一个退缩的身体。

branches.en: Small steps and weak smiles both show low confidence.
branches.cn: 小步子与勉强的笑容都透出底气不足。

intro.en: Timidly is built from the fear root tim- plus the English adverb suffix -ly, a partner of the adjectives and nouns in the family.
intro.cn: timidly 由表示恐惧的词根 tim- 加上英语副词后缀 -ly 构成，与同族的形容词、名词相互配合。

latinIntro.en: Latin timere means to fear; timidus is fearful, and English timid keeps that sense before the adverb ending -ly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 timere 意为害怕，timidus 意为胆小的，英语 timid 保留此义后再加副词后缀 -ly。

items.example: The root tim- recurs across the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 tim- 贯穿整个词族。

items.example: Timere supplies the family with fear.
items.exampleCN: timere 为词族提供「恐惧」之义。

items.example: Timidus develops into English timid.
items.exampleCN: timidus 发展出英语 timid。

items.example: Timid is the base of the adverb.
items.exampleCN: timid 是这个副词的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -ly makes timid into timidly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把 timid 变成 timidly。

items.example: Timidly describes the manner of an action.
items.exampleCN: timidly 描述动作的方式。

items.example: The Latin suffix -ity forms timidity from timid.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁后缀 -ity 把 timid 构成 timidity。

items.example: Timidity names the feeling behind timidly.
items.exampleCN: timidity 命名 timidly 背后的感受。

items.example: The prefix in- combines with timid to form intimidate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 与 timid 结合构成 intimidate。

items.example: Intimidate shares the fear root with timidly.
items.exampleCN: intimidate 与 timidly 共享恐惧词根。

definition_zh: 修补；摆弄；修理；小贩；瞎折腾
definition_en: to make small repairs or changes in an untrained, trial and error way
core_image: 老师傅蹲在台阶上，用一把小锤子叮叮当当地敲一只旧锅
scene: 后院的老收音机又不出声了，他把它拆开，用螺丝刀敲敲拧拧，终于找回了声音。He spent the afternoon tinkering with the old radio in the garage.
sceneCN: 这里 tinker 是「摆弄、修补」（第 1 个义项：做小修小补或反复调试）；句意：他整个下午都在车库里摆弄那台旧收音机。

pos.zh: 修补匠；走街串巷的小贩；瞎折腾

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 构成，义为「修修补补；小改动」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「爱摆弄东西的人」
同源拟声词 tinkle 加 -y 构成，义为「叮当作响的」
拟声动词，义为「叮当响；发出清脆声」，声音与 tinker 的敲打声同源

senses.title: To make small repairs
senses.definition: to try to repair or improve something by making small changes, often without proper tools or training
senses.definitionCN: 通过做小改动来尝试修理或改进某物，常用手边工具、不一定受过专业训练
senses.example: He likes to tinker with old bicycles in his spare time.
senses.exampleCN: 他业余时间喜欢摆弄旧自行车。
senses.why: The name of a travelling repairer gave a verb for that kind of small, repeated hammering work.
senses.whyCN: 走街串巷的修补匠的名称，变成了这种反复敲敲打打的小修小补动作的动词。

senses.title: To fiddle with plans or data
senses.definition: to keep changing a plan, system, or set of figures in a small but aimless way
senses.definitionCN: 以零碎而无明确方向的方式反复改动计划、系统或数据
senses.example: Stop tinkering with the budget and show us the final figures.
senses.exampleCN: 别再反复改预算了，把最终数字给我们看。
senses.why: The metal work stretches to ideas: a tinker moves small parts and never settles the whole.
senses.whyCN: 金属活儿的意象延伸到主意：摆弄者搬动的是小零件，整体却迟迟定不下来。

senses.title: A travelling mender and pedlar
senses.titleCN: 走街串巷的修补匠（兼小贩）
senses.definition: in older use, a person who travels from place to place mending pots and selling small goods
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指四处流动、补锅并兜售小商品的人
senses.example: The tinker mended our pots and sold us new spoons.
senses.exampleCN: 那位修补匠替我们补锅，还卖给我们新勺子。
senses.why: The noun keeps the historical person whose work gave the word its hammering image.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了历史上那个人：正是他的活儿，给这个词打下敲敲打打的意象。

senses.title: A wasted, restless effort
senses.definition: the act of working at something busily without useful results
senses.definitionCN: 忙碌地从事某事却没有有用成果的行为
senses.example: All that tinkering only made the engine worse.
senses.exampleCN: 那一通瞎鼓捣，反而让发动机更糟了。
senses.why: If you hammer away without knowing the cause, the effort itself becomes the noun.
senses.whyCN: 不知道毛病在哪却一直敲下去，这份努力本身就成了名词所指。

intro.en: Tinker is of uncertain origin; most likely it is an imitative word for repeated light metal taps, used first for a travelling mender, then for his work.
intro.cn: tinker 的来源不确定；一般认为它是摹仿反复轻敲金属声响的拟声词，先指流动的修补匠，再指他所干的活。

items.en: The word tinker is first recorded, naming a travelling mender of pots and pans.
items.cn: tinker 一词最早见于文献，指四处流动的补锅匠。

items.en: Northern and Scottish usage keeps the metal trade sense strongly.
items.cn: 苏格兰与英格兰北方用法中，打铁修器这层意思保留了很久。

items.en: The noun spreads the idea of small, clumsy repair work.
items.cn: 名词在十六世纪扩散出「零碎、笨拙的修修补补」这一含义。

items.en: The verb appears, meaning to mend or potter about with something.
items.cn: 动词义出现，意为修补或在一旁鼓捣。

items.en: Tinker now mostly means to adjust gadgets or systems, and the old trade noun is rare.
items.cn: 现代英语中 tinker 主要指摆弄设备或系统，旧时的职业名词已少见。

note.en: Tinker is a small-repair verb of imitative sound, sitting beside tinkle in form and beside fiddle and patch up in meaning.
note.cn: tinker 是带拟声色彩的「小修小补」动词，形式上与 tinkle 相邻，意义上与 fiddle、patch up 相近。

entries.definition: to make a light, clear ringing sound
to have an idea in mind
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写与读音接近，意为思考，词源不同

entries.definition: a person who enjoys making small repairs
to touch or adjust something restlessly
to repair something quickly and roughly
to fix something that is broken

normalIntro.en: Tinker sounds like light metal taps: a small hammer going ting, ting, ting on a pot.
normalIntro.cn: tinker 听起来就像金属被轻轻敲打：小锤子敲锅，发出叮叮叮的声响。

normal.en: To tinker with a machine is to tap at it, not to rebuild it.
normal.cn: tinker with a machine 是东敲敲西拧拧，而不是把它重造。

normal.en: Tinker is almost the sound of the job: ting, ting, ting.
normal.cn: tinker 几乎就是这活儿的声音：叮、叮、叮。

normal.en: A tinker historically was a travelling pot mender, so the verb means petty repair.
normal.cn: 历史上 tinker 是走街串巷的补锅匠，所以动词义是零碎修补。

normal.en: Compare tinkle: tinkle is the pretty ring, tinker is the busy work behind it.
normal.cn: 对比 tinkle：tinkle 是清脆的响声，tinker 是响声背后的忙活。

normal.en: Tinkering usually lacks skill, so people tinker in garages and sheds.
normal.cn: 摆弄往往不靠专业技术，所以人们总在车库和棚屋里 tinker。

abstract.en: Picture a hammer tapping a dented pot on a kitchen step.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小锤在厨房台阶上敲一只凹了的锅。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd of small screws moved from one side to the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆小螺丝被从这边挪到那边。

abstract.en: Think of a cart loaded with pots rolling from town to town.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆装满锅具的大车从一个镇子赶往另一个镇子。

examples.en: She tinkered with the settings for an hour before the printer worked.
examples.cn: 她摆弄了一个小时的设置，打印机才终于工作。

examples.en: Engineers are still tinkering with the design of the battery.
examples.cn: 工程师们仍在反复调整电池的设计。

examples.en: The old man tinkers in his shed every Sunday morning.
examples.cn: 那位老人每个星期天上午都在棚屋里鼓捣他的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「听客」——只顾低头听那叮叮当当的响声，手上不停敲敲拧拧；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定，一般认为拟声于反复轻敲金属的声响（与 tinkle 声音相近）；中古英语晚期指走街串巷的补锅匠，后引申为「小修小补、摆弄」，核心义「叮叮当当的小折腾」。

sensesIntro.en: Tinker begins as the name of a travelling pot mender, becomes the verb for small repairs, then spreads to fiddling with plans and to pointless busy effort.
sensesIntro.cn: tinker 先指流动的补锅匠，再作动词表示小修小补，进而扩展到反复改动方案，最后指白忙一场的折腾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small hammer tapping a dented pot on a kitchen step.
core.cn: 核心意象：小锤子在厨房台阶上敲一只凹了的锅。

branches.en: Small repair is the main verb sense.
branches.cn: 小修小补是主要的动词义项。

branches.en: Fiddling with plans is the figurative verb sense.
branches.cn: 反复改动计划是比喻性的动词义项。

branches.en: The travelling mender is the historical noun sense.
branches.cn: 流动的修补匠是历史上的名词义项。

branches.en: Busy but useless work is the critical noun sense.
branches.cn: 忙碌却无用的活儿是带批评意味的名词义项。

branches.en: The same tapping can be skilled repair or only wasted effort.
branches.cn: 同样的敲打，可能是熟练修补，也可能只是白费力气。

intro.en: Tinker has no certain Latin root; its parts are the imitative stem tink- and the English working endings -er, -ing, and -le.
intro.cn: tinker 没有确证的拉丁词根；其构成是拟声词干 tink- 加英语表示工作与动作的后缀 -er、-ing、-le。

latinIntro.en: No firm Latin source is known: the word is most likely an English imitation of light metal sound, so the list of Latin relatives is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 目前没有确证的拉丁语来源：这个词一般认为是对金属轻响的英语摹仿，因此拉丁同源词列表留空。

items.meaningCN: 金属被轻敲的清脆声响
items.example: The stem tink- echoes the sound of small hammering.
items.exampleCN: 词干 tink- 让人想到小锤轻敲的声音。

items.example: Tinkle keeps the pure sound meaning.
items.exampleCN: tinkle 保留了纯粹的声音含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示反复小动作的后缀
items.example: The ending -le marks a repeated light action in tinkle.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -le 在 tinkle 中标记反复的轻微动作。

items.meaningCN: 表示做某事之人的后缀
items.example: The suffix -er makes the trade name tinker.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成职业名称 tinker。

items.meaning: a mender, to mend in a small way
items.example: Tinker moves from a person to an action.
items.exampleCN: tinker 从指人转向指动作。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms the noun tinkering.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成名词 tinkering。

items.example: Tinkering is the gerund of the repair verb.
items.exampleCN: tinkering 是这一修补动词的动名词。

items.example: A tinkerer enjoys adjusting things in spare time.
items.exampleCN: tinkerer 指空闲时爱摆弄东西的人。

items.example: Tinkly describes a light, thin ringing.
items.exampleCN: tinkly 形容轻而细的响声。

items.meaning: the sound of a small bell
items.example: Ting is the plainest echo of a small bell.
items.exampleCN: ting 是对小铃铛声最直白的摹仿。

definition_zh: 耳鸣；耳边持续的嘶响或嗡嗡声
definition_en: a ringing, buzzing, or hissing sound heard in the ears or the head when there is no outside source
core_image: 四周明明安静，耳朵里却一直有一个细小的响声不停
scene: 阅览室里一片安静，有个学生却听见不知从哪里来的细响。In the hush of the reading room, a student heard a faint ringing from no speaker and asked the librarian about tinnitus.
sceneCN: 这里 tinnitus 是「耳鸣」（第 1 个义项：没有外部声源却听见响声）；句意：阅览室里一片安静，一名学生却听见不知来源的轻微鸣响，便向图书管理员询问耳鸣是怎么回事。

pos.zh: 耳鸣；耳朵或头内部无外部声源的持久响声

derivatives.zh: 耳部耳鸣的基础词加拉丁语属格 aurium（耳的）构成，是较旧的医学说法
基础词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「与耳鸣有关的」；少见说法，一般写作与 tinnitus 有关的
基础词加 masker（掩盖物）构成的复合词，指掩盖耳鸣声的装置

senses.title: The everyday ringing in the ears
senses.definition: the sense of hearing a ringing, buzzing, or hissing sound with no real sound outside the head
senses.definitionCN: 在没有外部真实声源的情况下听见铃声、嗡嗡声或嘶嘶声的感觉
senses.example: He has had tinnitus since he worked in a loud factory.
senses.exampleCN: 自从在吵闹的工厂工作以后，他就一直耳鸣。
senses.why: Latin tinnire describes a ringing sound, and tinnitus is the medical noun for hearing that ring with no outside cause.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tinnire 表示「发出铃样的响声」，tinnitus 就是把这种响声作为无外部来源的听觉体验来命名的医学名词，所以先长出「耳鸣」这一层日常含义。

senses.title: A persistent symptom left by noise
senses.titleCN: 噪声引起的持续性耳鸣
senses.definition: a lasting symptom, often caused by loud noise, ageing, or damage to the inner ear
senses.definitionCN: 多由强噪声、年龄增长或内耳损伤引起的长期症状
senses.example: Loud music at gigs is a common cause of tinnitus in young people.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会上过大的音量是年轻人耳鸣的常见原因。
senses.why: A ringing heard again and again becomes a lasting condition rather than a single event, so the word shifts from one sound to a chronic symptom.
senses.whyCN: 响声反复出现就不再是一次性的感受，而变成了长期状况；信标的画面于是从「听见一次铃响」滑向「持续的噪声后遗症」这一症状义。

senses.title: A clinical diagnosis and management aim
senses.definition: a diagnostic label that doctors assess, grade, and try to relieve with therapy
senses.definitionCN: 医生用来评估、分级并设法缓解的诊断名称
senses.example: The clinic offers sound therapy for patients with severe tinnitus.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为严重耳鸣的患者提供声治疗。
senses.why: Once a symptom is common and measurable, it is turned into a diagnosis that can be named and treated; the same noun now sits on a medical chart.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某种症状常见且可测量，它就会被变成可以命名、可以治疗的诊断；同一个名词随之出现在病历和处方上，长出临床义。

senses.title: The ringing without sound in literature
senses.definition: a literary and somewhat poetic use of a ringing that seems to come from inside the head
senses.definitionCN: 文学与略带诗意的用法，指仿佛来自头脑内部的铃声
senses.example: In the poem, tinnitus is the bell that rings when the world goes quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 在那首诗里，耳鸣就是世界安静下来时仍在响的钟。
senses.why: The tinnire image of a bell keeps a poetic charge, so writers can borrow the word to describe inner noise, memory, or loneliness.
senses.whyCN: tinnire 的「铃」意象本身带着诗意，作家便借用这个词去写内心的噪音、记忆或孤独，于是长出文学义。

senses.title: Objective tinnitus heard by a doctor
senses.definition: a rare form in which a doctor can actually hear the sound, often linked to blood flow or muscle near the ear
senses.definitionCN: 罕见的一类，医生用听诊器能真正听到声音，常与血流或耳周肌肉有关
senses.example: Pulsatile tinnitus can sometimes be objective tinnitus heard with a stethoscope.
senses.exampleCN: 搏动性耳鸣有时就是能用听诊器听到的客观性耳鸣。
senses.why: The general definition says there is no real sound, but a rare subgroup does produce a faint one, so clinicians split off a sub-sense that reverses that condition.
senses.whyCN: 基本定义强调「没有真实声源」，但少数病例确实能产生微弱可听的声音，医生便单独分出这一子义项，把「无声音」的条件反过来写。

senses.title: Ringing caused by drugs or injury
senses.titleCN: 药物或外伤导致的耳鸣
senses.definition: a ringing in the ears that follows certain medicines, head injury, or ear infection
senses.definitionCN: 由某些药物、头部外伤或耳部感染之后出现的耳鸣
senses.example: Some antibiotics are known to cause tinnitus as a side effect.
senses.exampleCN: 某些抗生素已知会带来耳鸣这一副作用。
senses.why: When doctors trace a ringing back to a drug or a blow to the head, the word becomes the name of that cause-effect link.
senses.whyCN: 当医生把耳鸣追查到某种药物或头部撞击时，这个词就成了那种因果关系的名字，长出「诱因型耳鸣」这一层。

senses.title: A ringing reported as a personal scale and impact
senses.titleCN: 作为主观困扰度与影响的耳鸣
senses.definition: the personal burden of the condition, as described on questionnaires about sleep, mood, and concentration
senses.definitionCN: 患者主观承受的困扰，用睡眠、情绪、注意力等问卷来描述
senses.example: On a scale of one to ten, her tinnitus affects her sleep at about eight.
senses.exampleCN: 按十分制打分，她的耳鸣对睡眠的影响大约有八分。
senses.why: Because no instrument can show another person the ringing, the word is re-read as how much it disturbs the listener, adding a measuring sense.
senses.whyCN: 因为没有仪器能向别人展示那声铃响，这个词就被重新理解为「对听者的干扰有多大」，于是多了一层衡量程度的义项。

intro.en: Tinnitus is a Latin medical word built on tinnire, to ring. English took it straight from Latin, and it still keeps the medical spelling with its double n.
intro.cn: tinnitus 是以拉丁语 tinnire（发出铃样的响声）为基础的拉丁医学词，英语直接借入，至今保留双 n 的医学拼写。

items.en: Tinnire means to ring or tinkle.
items.cn: tinnire 意为发出铃声或叮当声。

items.en: Tinnitus means a ringing, formed from tinnire and the abstract suffix -itus.
items.cn: tinnitus 意为「铃响」，由 tinnire 加抽象名词词尾 -itus 构成。

items.en: Writers pair it with aurium, of the ears, for clear medical use.
items.cn: 中世纪作者把它与表示「耳的」aurium 连用，使医学含义更明确。

items.en: Medical English borrows tinnitus as the term for a ringing with no sound outside.
items.cn: 十九世纪医学英语借用 tinnitus，专指没有外部声源的铃响。

items.en: The word spreads beyond clinics into hearing safety, music, and public health.
items.cn: 现代英语把这词从诊室带到听力保护、音乐与公共卫生领域。

note.en: Tinnitus sits in the hearing family by meaning, and shares a bell image with tint and tintinnabulation by sound; those relatives only look or sound alike.
note.cn: tinnitus 按意义属于「听觉」词汇家族，按声音与 tint、tintinnabulation 共享「铃」意象；这些只是形近音近，不是同源同义。

entries.definition: the ringing sound of bells
entries.definitionCN: 铃声响动；与 tinnitus 同出拉丁语 tinnire

entries.definition: a pale shade of colour
entries.definitionCN: 淡色调；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 tingere

entries.definition: the state of being tense or stretched
entries.definitionCN: 紧张；紧拉的状态；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a bell-like sound, often heard inside the ears
entries.definitionCN: 铃声；常指耳内听到的响声

entries.definition: a low humming sound like a bee
entries.definitionCN: 嗡嗡声；像蜜蜂一样的低鸣

entries.definition: a reduced ability to hear, often linked to tinnitus
entries.definitionCN: 听力下降；常与耳鸣并存

normalIntro.en: Tinnitus comes from the Latin verb for ringing, so a reliable way to hold the word is to tie it to bells and to the sounds ears make.
normalIntro.cn: tinnitus 源自拉丁语「铃响」动词，最可靠的记法是把这个词系在钟铃和耳朵里自发的响声上。

normal.en: Tinnire, the Latin root, means to ring, so tinnitus is the ringing itself.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 tinnire 意为鸣响，所以 tinnitus 就是那声铃响本身。

normal.en: Tintinnabulation is a cousin word: bells tintinnabulate, ears hear tinnitus.
normal.cn: tintinnabulation 是它的表亲词：铃铛叮当作响，耳朵听见耳鸣。

normal.en: Suffer from tinnitus is the standard verb phrase in health writing.
normal.cn: 「suffer from tinnitus」是健康写作中的标准动词搭配。

normal.en: Chronic tinnitus is the set phrase for the long-lasting form.
normal.cn: chronic tinnitus 是表达长期耳鸣的固定说法。

normal.en: Clinics speak of tinnitus relief and tinnitus maskers.
normal.cn: 诊所会说 tinnitus relief（缓解耳鸣）与 tinnitus masker（耳鸣掩盖器）。

abstract.en: Picture a small silver bell ringing inside your skull while the room is silent.
abstract.cn: 想象房间寂静无声，一只小小的银铃却在你的头骨里响。

abstract.en: Picture a wince after the amp, then the same ring still there at night.
abstract.cn: 想象听完大音箱后皱着眉，到了夜里同一阵鸣响还在。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor writing the word on a chart and circling it.
abstract.cn: 想象医生在病历上写下这个词，再把它圈起来。

examples.en: Loud concerts can leave young people with tinnitus for days.
examples.cn: 吵闹的演出会让年轻人连日耳鸣。

examples.en: She uses a white noise app to make her tinnitus less noticeable.
examples.cn: 她用白噪声应用让耳鸣不那么明显。

examples.en: The doctor asked how long the tinnitus had lasted.
examples.cn: 医生询问耳鸣持续了多久。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「听你头死」——听你自己脑袋里的死命响声，就是耳鸣；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tinnire（铃样鸣响）+ 名词词尾 -itus → 拉丁医学名词 tinnitus（铃响）→ 英语 tinnitus（耳鸣）；词根可靠，首见年代存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Tinnitus starts from one concrete image, a bell ringing with no outside cause, and branches into a symptom, a diagnosis, a poetic image, and a measure of personal burden.
sensesIntro.cn: tinnitus 从一个具体意象出发——没有外部声源却响起的铃——再分出症状、诊断、文学想象与主观困扰程度等义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bell ringing inside a quiet head.
core.cn: 核心意象：安静的头脑里有一只小铃在响。

branches.en: Everyday ear ringing is the plain sense from the root image.
branches.cn: 日常的耳内鸣响，是核心意象最直接的义项。

branches.en: When noise or a drug starts the ringing, it becomes a lasting symptom with a cause.
branches.cn: 当噪声或药物引发鸣响，它就变成有诱因的持续症状。

branches.en: Diagnosis, the rare audible form, and the personal burden are all clinical readings.
branches.cn: 诊断、罕见的可听型与主观困扰程度，都属于临床解读。

branches.en: Literature turns the same inner bell into a symbol of loneliness.
branches.cn: 文学把同一只内心的铃变成孤独的象征。

branches.en: Both the everyday and the poetic sense describe a sound heard only inside.
branches.cn: 日常义与文学义都描述只在内部听见的声音。

intro.en: Tinnitus has no English prefix or suffix of its own; its parts are all Latin, and English mainly adds compound words about hearing health.
intro.cn: tinnitus 本身没有英语前缀或后缀，各部件都来自拉丁语，英语主要在它外面加与听力健康有关的复合说法。

latinIntro.en: Latin tinnire gives the ringing verb, and the abstract suffix -itus turns the sound into a noun name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tinnire 提供「鸣响」的动词，抽象词尾 -itus 把这个声音变成名词名称。

items.example: The stem tinn- appears in tinnire and tinnitus.
items.exampleCN: 词干 tinn- 出现在 tinnire 与 tinnitus 中。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或动作的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -itus names the act of ringing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -itus 把「鸣响」这个动作变成名称。

items.example: Tinnire is the direct root.
items.exampleCN: tinnire 是直接词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示「充满……的」的拉丁词尾
items.example: The Latin suffix -osus marks something full of a quality.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁词尾 -osus 表示充满某种性质。

items.example: The suffix -al forms a rare adjective such as tinnital.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 tinnital 这类少见形容词。

items.example: A tinnitus masker hides the ringing with soft sound.
items.exampleCN: 耳鸣掩盖器用柔和的声音遮住鸣响。

items.example: The Latin root aur- means ear.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁词根 aur- 表示耳朵。

items.example: Tintinnabulum shares the same ringing stem.
items.exampleCN: tintinnabulum 共享同一个「鸣响」词干。

items.example: The ending -ae marks possession as in ear of.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ae 表示所属关系。

latinEntries.example: Tinnire is the source of the noun.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tinnire 是这一名词的来源。

latinEntries.example: The bell noun shares the ringing image.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 表示铃的名词共享鸣响意象。

definition_zh: 淡色调；给……淡淡地上色；染发剂
definition_en: a pale or slight shade of colour, or to give something such a colour
core_image: 一层极薄的颜色像轻纱一样覆在原本的底色上
scene: 画家怕画面太白，往颜料里兑了一点点蓝。The painter added a faint blue tint to the white paint so the wall would look warmer.
sceneCN: 这里 tint 是「淡色调」（第 1 个义项：很浅的一层颜色）；句意：画家在白色颜料里兑了一点淡淡的蓝色调，好让墙面看起来更暖。

pos.zh: 给……淡淡地上色；使带上某种色彩倾向

derivatives.zh: 基础词加过去分词词尾 -ed 构成，义为「染了色的；带色镜片的」
基础词加 -ing 构成名词，义为「上色；镜片着色」
基础词加施动者词尾 -er 构成，指「调色剂；上色的人」

senses.title: A pale shade of colour
senses.definition: a colour that is very light or is mixed with white, so that it only slightly changes the base colour
senses.definitionCN: 一种很浅的颜色，或掺了白色、只轻微改变底色的颜色
senses.example: The sky turned a pale pink tint at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时天空泛起一层淡粉色。
senses.why: Latin tingere means to dip or dye, and early use of the word names any dye colour, which settles into the idea of a light, thin, added colour.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tingere 意为浸染，这个词最初指任何染料颜色，后来沉淀为「浅淡、轻薄、附加」的一层颜色，于是长出「淡色调」义。

senses.title: A small trace of a quality
senses.definition: a very small amount of a feeling or quality that colours something else
senses.definitionCN: 某种情感或性质的一点点痕迹，像颜色一样给别的事物染上一层意味
senses.example: There was a tint of irony in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音里带着一丝反讽的意味。
senses.why: Once a tint is a thin layer on a surface, it easily moves from covers to character, so a light colour becomes a light trace of an attitude.
senses.whyCN: 一旦淡色是覆在表面的一层薄膜，它就很容易从「覆在物体上」过渡到「覆在性质上」：淡淡的颜色变成淡淡的态度痕迹，这就是引申义。

senses.title: The act of giving a light colour
senses.definition: the action of applying a light colour, especially to glass, film, or hair
senses.definitionCN: 给玻璃、胶片或头发轻轻着色的动作
senses.example: The tinting of the office windows cuts down the glare.
senses.exampleCN: 给办公室窗户着色能减轻刺眼的光。
senses.why: The dip-and-dye verb inside the root comes forward again, and the noun names the act of putting that layer on.
senses.whyCN: 词根里「浸染」的动作重新浮现出来，于是名词可以指「把这一层颜色加上去」这个动作本身。

senses.title: Hair dye in a light shade
senses.definition: a product or a light shade used to give hair a gentle colour
senses.definitionCN: 为头发上浅色、自然颜色的染发产品
senses.example: She used a henna tint instead of a permanent dye.
senses.exampleCN: 她用的是指甲花染发剂，而不是永久性染发。
senses.why: Hair colour is sold as a light cover rather than a total repaint, so the product takes the name of the thin layer it leaves.
senses.whyCN: 染发剂卖的往往是一层浅浅的覆盖，而不是彻底重刷，所以产品直接借用它所留下的薄层之名，形成染发剂义。

senses.title: A coloured lens layer
senses.definition: a coloured coating on a lens or film that changes the light or the picture
senses.definitionCN: 镜片或胶片上的有色涂层，用来改变透过的光或画面效果
senses.example: The camera lens has a blue tint to balance daylight.
senses.exampleCN: 相机镜头有一层蓝色镀层，用来平衡日光。
senses.why: Glass with a thin metal layer lets light pass on its terms, so technicians call that layer a tint too.
senses.whyCN: 镀了薄层的玻璃按自己的方式筛选光线，技术人员便把这一薄层也称作 tint，由此分出镜片色层义。

senses.title: A graphic layer that adds colour
senses.definition: in art and computing, a layer of colour applied over a picture or image to change its feel
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画与图像处理中，覆盖在画面上以改变色调感的一层颜色
senses.example: The designer put a warm tint over the photo.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师在照片上叠加了一层暖色。
senses.why: Any image editing step that lays colour over the whole picture repeats the original gesture of dipping colour over a base, so the word fits screens too.
senses.whyCN: 任何在整个画面上加一层颜色的修图步骤，都是「往底子上蘸一层色」这一原初动作的重复，所以这个词也适用于屏幕。

senses.title: A colour that belongs to a place or era
senses.definition: a characteristic colour that comes from a particular place, season, or period
senses.definitionCN: 某地、某个季节或某个时代特有的颜色
senses.example: The photos show the dusty silver tint of winter in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 照片呈现出北方冬天那种灰扑扑的银色调。
senses.why: When the same faint colour repeats over a whole landscape or era, people start using the word for the mood given by that light.
senses.whyCN: 当同一种淡淡的颜色反复出现在整片风景或整个时代上时，人们便把那种光线带来的氛围也称作一种 tint。

senses.title: A printing plate colour
senses.definition: in printing, a lighter screen of a solid ink used to create lighter shades of one colour
senses.definitionCN: 印刷中把专色网点做稀，用来产生同一颜色的更浅层次
senses.example: The leaflet used a fifty per cent tint of the company blue.
senses.exampleCN: 传单用了公司蓝色五成的网点色。
senses.why: Printing cannot mix white into ink easily, so it makes a colour lighter by screening it; the screened colour keeps the word for a light shade.
senses.whyCN: 印刷不便把白墨混进油墨，于是靠网点把颜色做淡；这种网屏色正好对应「淡色调」这一基本义，印刷术语便沿用下来。

senses.title: To give something a light colour
senses.definition: to give something a slight or pale colour, so that the base colour still shows
senses.definitionCN: 给某物加上浅浅的颜色，使原来的底色仍然透出来
senses.example: The sunset tinted the clouds orange.
senses.exampleCN: 夕阳把云朵染成了橙色。
senses.why: The verb is the root action itself: to dip or dye, but always lightly, which is why tint suggests a gentle change of colour.
senses.whyCN: 动词义就是词根的原始动作「浸染」，只是力度很轻，所以 tint 作动词时暗示的是温和的变色。

senses.title: To influence how something is judged
senses.definition: to colour a judgement or memory slightly, so that it is no longer purely neutral
senses.definitionCN: 给某个判断或记忆染上一点色彩，使它不再完全中立
senses.example: The memory was tinted with regret.
senses.exampleCN: 那段记忆染上了悔意。
senses.why: The light-colour verb is stretched to feelings: a view can be tinted by emotion just as a window is tinted by film.
senses.whyCN: 「淡淡上色」这个动词被拉伸到情感上：看法会像玻璃贴膜那样被情绪染上一层薄色，于是长出判断受影响的义项。

intro.en: Tint comes from Latin tingere, to dip or dye, through the Italian verb tintare and its noun tinta, which gave English both the verb and the noun.
intro.cn: tint 来自拉丁语 tingere（浸染），经意大利语动词 tintare 及其名词 tinta 进入英语，同时带来动词与名词两种词性。

items.en: Tingere means to dip something in colour, to dye or soak.
items.cn: tingere 意为把某物浸入颜料中，即浸染、浸透。

items.en: The noun tinctura, a dyeing, is built from the same stem.
items.cn: 同一词干还构成名词 tinctura，意为染色。

items.en: The verb tintare and its noun tinta mean to dye and a dye.
items.cn: 意大利语动词 tintare 与名词 tinta，分别意为染色与染料。

items.en: English borrows tint as a noun for a colour or shade.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借用 tint 作名词，指颜色或色调。

items.en: The verb sense, to give a light colour, becomes common.
items.cn: 十九世纪，tint 作动词表示「淡淡上色」的用法变得常见。

items.en: The word spreads to glass, photography, printing, and screens.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词扩展到玻璃、摄影、印刷与屏幕。

note.en: Tint stays close to its Latin cousins tinge and tincture in form, and to shade, hue, and dye in meaning; those words differ in whether they name a colour, a tone, or an action.
note.cn: tint 在形式上与同源的 tinge、tincture 相近，在意义上与 shade、hue、dye 相邻；这些词的区别在于各自指的是颜色、色调还是动作。

entries.definition: thin shiny strips used as decoration
entries.definitionCN: 光彩闪亮的装饰箔片；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自古法语 estincelle

entries.definition: a small amount of a colour
entries.definitionCN: 一丝颜色；与 tint 同出拉丁语 tingere

entries.definition: a medicine or colouring made from a liquid infusion
a particular form of a colour, darker or lighter than a base one
entries.definitionCN: 色调；同一种颜色的深浅变化；比 tint 更强调深浅层次

entries.definition: the basic character of a colour
entries.definitionCN: 色彩；色调；更书面，强调颜色的基本性质

entries.definition: a substance or action that gives a strong colour
entries.definitionCN: 染料；染色；着色比 tint 更浓更彻底

normalIntro.en: Tint belongs to the Latin family of dip and dye, so link it to tinge and tincture, and remember that it always means a light, thin colour.
normalIntro.cn: tint 属于拉丁语「浸染」词族，可以把它和 tinge、tincture 放在一起记，并记住它总表示淡淡的一层颜色。

normal.en: Tingere, to dip in dye, is the root, so a tint is the thin layer of colour a dip leaves.
normal.cn: 词根 tingere 是「浸入染料」，所以 tint 就是浸一下留下的薄薄一层色。

normal.en: Tinge and tincture are its cousins, both about a light touch of colour.
normal.cn: tinge 与 tincture 是它的表亲词，说的都是一点点颜色的轻触。

normal.en: Tinted glasses and tinted windows are the everyday compounds.
normal.cn: tinted glasses 与 tinted windows 是日常复合搭配。

normal.en: A hair tint is a gentle dye, never a complete repaint.
normal.cn: hair tint 是温和的染发，而不是彻底重刷。

normal.en: Shade is about light and dark, tint is about pale and thin.
normal.cn: shade 讲深浅，tint 讲浅淡与轻薄，两个词的分工要分清。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of blue ink spreading through a glass of white milk.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴蓝墨在一杯白牛奶里慢慢散开。

abstract.en: Picture a voice smiling with just a hint of irony.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音里带着一丝反讽的笑意。

abstract.en: Picture a roller gliding a pale film over a tall window.
abstract.cn: 想象一把滚刷把淡色的薄膜刷过一整扇高窗。

examples.en: The evening light gave the room a golden tint.
examples.cn: 傍晚的光把房间染成金黄。

examples.en: He tinted the glass panels to keep the office cooler.
examples.cn: 他给玻璃板上了色，让办公室更凉快。

examples.en: Her usually calm reply had a faint tint of annoyance.
examples.cn: 她一向平静的回答里带上了一丝不快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「T 一 T 一点点」——只往颜料里 T 一点点，就是淡淡的色调；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tingere（浸染）→ 同一词干构成 tinctura → 意大利语 tintare、tinta → 英语 tint（淡色调；上色）；词根可靠，首见年代一般认为在十八世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Tint keeps one image, a thin pale layer over a base colour, and grows into a trace of feeling, an action, hair dye, a lens layer, and finally a way of colouring a judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: tint 守着一个意象——蒙在底色上的一层淡色薄层，并由此长出情感痕迹、着色动作、染发剂、镜片色层以及给判断染色的义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin film of pale colour laid over what is already there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层淡色的薄纱盖在原有底色之上。

branches.en: A pale colour and a place or season colour are both visible light layers.
branches.cn: 淡色调与地区季节色彩，都是看得见的浅色层。

branches.en: A trace of feeling and a tinted judgement extend the light colour to character.
branches.cn: 一丝意味与被染色的判断，把浅色从颜色延伸到性格与看法。

branches.en: The action sense and the verb repeat the root gesture of lightly dipping or dyeing.
branches.cn: 名词的动作义与动词义，都是词根「轻轻浸染」手势的重现。

branches.en: Hair colour and lens coating are products that leave a thin colour layer.
branches.cn: 染发剂与镜片镀膜，都是会留下薄色层的产品。

branches.en: Graphic tint layers and printing tints are technical copies of the same idea.
branches.cn: 图像叠加色与印刷网点色，是同一观念的技术版本。

intro.en: Tint has almost no English affixes inside it: the whole word is the Latin dyeing stem, and English adds endings such as -ed, -ing, and -er to make new words.
intro.cn: tint 内部几乎没有英语词缀：整个词就是拉丁语「染色」词干，英语在它后面加 -ed、-ing、-er 等词尾造出新词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tingere is the dyeing root; it also gives tincture, tinge, and many technical colour words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tingere 是表示「染色」的词根，它还带来 tincture、tinge 以及许多专业技术词。

items.example: The stem ting- carries the dipping image.
items.exampleCN: 词干 ting- 承载「浸入」的意象。

items.example: The ending -ere marks the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ere 标示拉丁动词。

items.example: Tingere is the ancestor of tint.
items.exampleCN: tingere 是 tint 的祖先。

items.example: Tinctura shows the same stem as a noun.
items.exampleCN: tinctura 用同一词干构成名词。

items.example: Tinta is the form English took.
items.exampleCN: 英语借的就是 tinta 这个词形。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms tinted.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 tinted。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms tinting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 tinting。

items.example: The suffix -er forms tinter.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 tinter。

items.example: The variant stem tinct- appears in tincture.
items.exampleCN: 变体词干 tinct- 出现在 tincture 中。

latinEntries.example: Tinctura is the Latin noun of the same stem.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tinctura 是同词干的拉丁名词。
分词 tinctus 意为染过的。

definition_zh: 钛；（用于高强度结构的）金属钛材料
definition_en: a strong, light, silver-grey metal that resists rust and is used in aircraft, medical implants, and everyday goods
core_image: 一块银灰色、轻得出奇却极难折断的金属
scene: 工程师在做飞机零件选材，最看重的两点是轻和结实。The engineer chose titanium for the landing gear because it stays strong while being much lighter than steel.
sceneCN: 这里 titanium 是「钛」（第 1 个义项：一种轻而坚固的金属元素）；句意：工程师为起落架选用钛，因为它依然坚固，却比钢轻得多。

pos.zh: 钛（化学元素）；（用于结构的）钛材

derivatives.zh: 同出希腊泰坦词根，义为「巨大的」；与钛的关联主要在命名上
基础词加 dioxide（二氧化物）构成，是一种白色颜料与防晒成分
基础词的词干加 -ate 构成，指钛酸盐类化合物
基础词的词干加 -iferous（含有……的）构成，义为「含钛的」

senses.title: The metal element
senses.definition: a lightweight, very strong, silver-grey metal that does not rust easily
senses.definitionCN: 一种轻、强度很高、银灰色且不易生锈的金属
senses.example: Titanium is light, strong, and hard to corrode.
senses.exampleCN: 钛既轻又强，还不易腐蚀。
senses.why: The word is a modern chemical name created from the Greek race of giants, so its first sense is simply the element itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是现代化学命名的产物，取自希腊神话中夸父般的泰坦巨人；因此第一个义项就是这种元素本身，名字自带「巨大力量」的联想。

senses.title: The metal chosen in aviation
senses.definition: titanium used in aircraft and spacecraft because it keeps strength while saving weight
senses.definitionCN: 用于飞机与航天器，因其在减轻重量时仍能保持强度
senses.example: Aircraft makers use titanium in the hottest parts of the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机制造商在发动机最热的部位使用钛。
senses.why: The element is worth naming in its own right only because of its lab performance, so the practical aviation use grows straight out of the characteristic of being light and strong.
senses.whyCN: 这种元素之所以值得单独命名，全靠它的性能；「又轻又结实」这个特性直接生出航空用途的含义。

senses.title: Titanium in the body
senses.definition: metal used in hip joints, dental screws, and other implants because the body tolerates it
senses.definitionCN: 因人体对其耐受性好而用于髋关节、牙种植体等植入物
senses.example: The surgeon replaced the damaged joint with a titanium implant.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生用钛植入体替换了受损的关节。
senses.why: Bones and tissue can live beside titanium without rejecting it, so the same metal gains a medical identity.
senses.whyCN: 骨骼与组织能与钛共处而不排斥它，于是同一种金属又获得了医学上的身份。

senses.title: The white pigment compounds
senses.definition: titanium dioxide, the bright white substance used in paint, paper, plastic, and sunscreen
senses.definitionCN: 二氧化钛，用作涂料、纸张、塑料与防晒品的亮白色物质
senses.example: The sunscreen lists titanium dioxide as its active filter.
senses.exampleCN: 这款防晒霜把二氧化钛列为主要防晒成分。
senses.why: Titanium compounds scatter light very strongly, so the element name moves out of the metal and into the white powder made from it.
senses.whyCN: 钛的化合物对光散射极强，于是这个元素名从金属本身迁移到由它制成的白色粉末上。

senses.title: Gadgets that feel metal and modern
senses.definition: products such as frames, watches, bottles, and clubs advertised as made of titanium
senses.definitionCN: 眼镜框、手表、水瓶、高尔夫球杆等标榜用钛制成的产品
senses.example: He bought a titanium frame because it would not rust.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一副钛镜框，因为它不会生锈。
senses.why: Once a metal is rare and strong, its name becomes a selling point, so titanium turns into a label for goods that claim that quality.
senses.whyCN: 一种又稀有又结实的金属，名字本身就成卖点；于是钛从一个元素变成商品上标榜性能的标签。

senses.title: The word as a sign of strength
senses.definition: a figurative use in which titanium stands for toughness, endurance, or a hardened attitude
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性用法，用钛代指坚韧、耐用或强硬的态度
senses.example: Her advice was wrapped in titanium: direct, calm, and impossible to dent.
senses.exampleCN: 她的建议像包着钛一样：直接、冷静，刀枪不入。
senses.why: The metal resists bending and scratching, and that picture is easily lent to people and to arguments.
senses.whyCN: 这种金属抗弯抗划，这个画面很容易被借来形容人和论点，于是长出比喻义。

senses.title: The Greek Titans behind the name
senses.definition: the Greek gods of enormous power whose name was borrowed for the metal and its wider family
senses.definitionCN: 希腊神话中力量巨大的神族，其名字被借用来给这种金属及同族词命名
senses.example: The name titanium points back to the Titans of Greek myth.
senses.exampleCN: titanium 这个名字可以回溯到希腊神话中的泰坦。
senses.why: The chemist who named the element reached for the Titans to say that this metal would be mighty, so the myth stays inside the word.
senses.whyCN: 命名这种元素的化学家借用泰坦之名，是想说这种金属会非常强大；神话因此一直留在词里。

intro.en: Titanium is a modern scientific name. It was coined from Greek Titanes, the Titans, by the chemist Martin Heinrich Klaproth after titanium oxide was identified in 1791.
intro.cn: titanium 是现代科学命名，由化学家克拉普罗特在鉴定出二氧化钛之后，用希腊语 Titanes（泰坦神族）造出，一般认为在十八世纪末。

items.en: The Titanes are the older race of gods in Greek myth.
items.cn: Titanes 是希腊神话中古老的泰坦神族。

items.en: Latin Titan keeps the Greek name and gives the form used by scholars.
items.cn: 拉丁语 Titan 保留希腊原名，并提供学者使用的词形。

items.en: Chemists use the metal name titanion for the oxide they found.
items.cn: 化学家把发现的氧化物称为 titanion，取自泰坦之名。

items.en: Klaproth names the element titanium, modelled on other metal names such as uranium.
items.cn: 克拉普罗特仿照 uranium 等金属名，把该元素命名为 titanium。

items.en: Commercial refining brings the metal into aircraft, medicine, and household goods.
items.cn: 二十世纪工业化提炼让这种金属进入飞机、医学与日用品。

note.en: Titanium looks and sounds like its own Latin cousins tantalum and titanate, and it belongs in meaning to the family of light strong metals.
note.cn: titanium 在拼写与读音上与同源的 tantalum、titanate 相近（只是相似，并非同义），在意义上则属于「轻而坚固的金属」这一家族。

entries.definition: a hard grey metal used in electronics
entries.definitionCN: 钽；一种坚硬的稀有金属，常与钛相伴开采；拼写相近，元素不同

entries.definition: a salt or compound of titanium
entries.definitionCN: 钛酸盐；由钛的化合物派生

entries.definition: a giant in Greek myth, or a person of great power
entries.definitionCN: 希腊神话中的泰坦巨神；与目标词同源，是命名来源

entries.definition: a light silver metal used in cans and aircraft
entries.definitionCN: 铝；同样轻质、常用于飞机

entries.definition: a metal made by mixing two or more metals
entries.definitionCN: 合金；钛常以合金形式使用

entries.definition: a corrosion-resistant metal used in reactors and dental work
entries.definitionCN: 锆；同样耐腐蚀，也用于牙科

normalIntro.en: Titanium is named after the Greek Titans, and its chemical symbol is Ti, so the name itself tells you it is about strength.
normalIntro.cn: titanium 得名于希腊泰坦，化学符号是 Ti；名字本身就在提示「力量」。

normal.en: The Greek Titans were giants, so titanium is the giant metal, light in weight but mighty.
normal.cn: 希腊泰坦是巨人，所以 titanium 就是「巨人的金属」，轻却有大力。

normal.en: The chemical symbol Ti marks two sets of forms: the -um ending and the -ic ending.
normal.cn: 化学符号 Ti 提示两组词形：以 -um 结尾的 titanium 与以 -ic 结尾的 titanic。

normal.en: Titanium dioxide is the white pigment on every sunscreen label.
normal.cn: titanium dioxide 是每支防晒霜标签上的白色颜料。

normal.en: A titanium implant is chosen because the body accepts the metal.
normal.cn: 选钛植入体，是因为人体能接受这种金属。

normal.en: Compare aluminium: both are light metals, but titanium holds its strength at high heat.
normal.cn: 对比 aluminium：两者都是轻金属，但钛在高温下仍能保持强度。

abstract.en: Picture a silver bar so light that it floats in water, yet so hard that a hammer bounces off.
abstract.cn: 想象一块银色的金属轻得能浮在水面，却硬得让锤子弹开。

abstract.en: Picture a jet engine glowing red while its fan blades stay straight.
abstract.cn: 想象喷气发动机烧得发红，风扇叶片却依旧笔直。

abstract.en: Picture a dentist showing a small screw that locks into bone.
abstract.cn: 想象牙医举起一颗能牢牢锁进骨头的小螺钉。

examples.en: Titanium resists salt water better than most steel.
examples.cn: 钛比大多数钢材更耐海水侵蚀。

examples.en: The watch is advertised as titanium, so it feels very light on the wrist.
examples.cn: 这款手表标榜是钛制的，所以戴在手腕上非常轻。

examples.en: Researchers tested a titanium coating for the hip implant.
examples.cn: 研究人员为髋关节植入体测试了一种钛涂层。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「钛轻，抬得动」——又轻又结实，抬得动也压不弯；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 Titanes（泰坦神族）→ 拉丁语 Titan → 十八世纪末化学家用泰坦之名造出 titanium（钛）；词根可靠，具体命名年份说法不一。

sensesIntro.en: Titanium moves from the element to its strong light uses in aircraft, its medical acceptance in the body, its white compounds, its promises on products, and finally its figurative meaning as strength.
sensesIntro.cn: titanium 从元素本身出发，走向航空中的轻强用途、人体中的医用相容性、白色化合物、商品上的性能标签，最后变成「坚韧」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver bar that is absurdly light and almost impossible to dent.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块轻得离谱、几乎砸不坏的银色金属。

branches.en: The element itself is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 元素本身是最直接的义项。

branches.en: Light yet strong makes the metal wanted in aircraft and in gadgets.
branches.cn: 轻而强，使这种金属成为航空与日用品争抢的材料。

branches.en: The body tolerating the metal gives the implant sense.
branches.cn: 人体能耐受这种金属，长出植入体义项。

branches.en: The white compounds are the pigment sense.
branches.cn: 白色化合物构成颜料义项。

branches.en: The mythical giant stays behind the figurative strength sense.
branches.cn: 神话中的巨人留在「坚韧」比喻义的背后。

intro.en: Titanium is a coined scientific word: a Greek myth name plus -ium, the modern suffix for metals, and English keeps building on it.
intro.cn: titanium 是人为造出的科学词：希腊神话名字加上表示金属的现代词尾 -ium，英语又在它基础上继续造词。

latinIntro.en: Latin Titan, from Greek Titanes, supplies the name, and the Latin-style -ium marks a metal, as in uranium and aluminium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Titan（来自希腊语 Titanes）提供词干，拉丁式词尾 -ium 标示金属，如 uranium 与 aluminium。

items.example: The stem Titan- doubles as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词干 Titan- 也可作形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ium marks a metal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ium 标示金属。

items.example: Titanic describes size.
items.exampleCN: titanic 描述体积。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms titanate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 titanate。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms titanic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 titanic。

items.example: The suffix -ous appears in titanium compound names.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 出现在钛的化合物名称中。

items.meaning: an oxide with one oxygen pair
items.example: Dioxide joins titanium in the white pigment.
items.exampleCN: dioxide 与 titanium 组成白色颜料的名称。

items.example: The symbol Ti marks titanium on the periodic table.
items.exampleCN: 符号 Ti 在元素周期表上标示钛。

items.example: The suffix -iferous forms titaniferous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -iferous 构成 titaniferous。

latinEntries.example: Latin Titan carries the myth name onward.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 Titan 把这个神话名传下来。

latinEntries.example: The Greek form supplies the stem.

definition_zh: 蟾蜍；癞蛤蟆；讨厌的人
definition_en: a small fat animal with dry warty skin that lives on land and hops rather than jumps
core_image: 一只蹲在潮湿石缝里、皮肤粗糙起疙瘩的蟾蜍
scene: 雨后的花园里，一只蟾蜍从石头下慢慢爬出来。After the rain, a toad crept out from under the garden stone.
sceneCN: 这里 toad 是「蟾蜍」（第 1 个义项：皮肤粗糙、多在陆地活动的两栖动物）；句意：雨后的花园里，一只蟾蜍从石头下慢慢爬出来。

collocations.zh: 长着蟾蜍般脑袋的（多用于童话插图的形容）
蟾蜍和青蛙（常并列出现）
蟾蜍毒液（中药、药学文献用语）

derivatives.zh: 由 toad 加 stool（凳子）构成，指菌盖下有毒的蘑菇，民间传说蟾蜍坐上去
由 toad 加 -y 构成，指谄媚讨好的人，源自古时江湖郎中吃蟾蜍的随从
由 toad 加 fish 构成，指体形笨重、叫声粗哑的蟾鱼
由 toad 加 -like（像……的）构成，形容像蟾蜍那样

senses.title: A warty amphibian that lives on land
senses.definition: a small fat amphibian with dry, warty skin that mostly lives on land and hops
senses.definitionCN: 一种体小肥胖、皮肤干燥起疙瘩的两栖动物，多生活在陆地上，以跳步移动
senses.example: A toad sat still under the wet stone.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蟾蜍一动不动地蹲在湿石头下面。
senses.why: English toad is a word of unknown origin generally compared with Dutch and German forms for a warty jumping creature; the skin and the land habit are the picture.
senses.whyCN: 英语 toad 来源不确定，一般认为与荷兰语、德语中表示疙瘩皮跳跃小动物的词同系；起疙瘩的皮与陆地习性正是它的画面。

senses.title: The dry-skinned cousin of the frog
senses.titleCN: 与青蛙相对的旱地类群
senses.definition: the frog family member that is drier, thicker, and slower, usually walking or hopping instead of leaping
senses.definitionCN: 青蛙一类中更干燥、更粗壮、更迟缓的成员，通常爬行或短跳而不是远跳
senses.example: Frogs prefer ponds, while toads can live in dry fields.
senses.exampleCN: 青蛙喜欢待在池塘，而蟾蜍能生活在干燥的田野里。
senses.why: Once toad named this creature, speakers used it to contrast with frog, so the word also marks the land-dwelling side of the pair.
senses.whyCN: toad 一旦用来称呼这种动物，人们就拿它和 frog 对照，于是这个词也标出了「成群对照中偏旱地的那一方」。

senses.title: An ugly or spiteful person
senses.titleCN: 讨厌的人；丑态可憎的人
senses.definition: an insulting word for someone considered ugly, spiteful, or repulsive
senses.definitionCN: 对人刻薄或丑陋之人的贬称
senses.example: The old toad never returns what he borrows.
senses.exampleCN: 那个讨厌的老家伙从不归还借来的东西。
senses.why: The animal own rough skin and squat shape carry a folk image of ugliness, so the name was transferred to disliked people.
senses.whyCN: 蟾蜍粗糙的皮肤和蹲伏的体形带着民间「丑」的印象，于是这个词被转用来指不受欢迎的人。

senses.title: The transformed prince in fairy tales
senses.titleCN: 童话里被变成蟾蜍的角色
senses.definition: a figure in traditional stories who has been changed into a toad and waits to be freed
senses.definitionCN: 传统故事中被魔法变成蟾蜍、等待解除的角色
senses.example: In the old tale, a prince was turned into a toad.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个古老的故事里，一位王子被变成了蟾蜍。
senses.why: Folktales use the plain animal as a disguise for a hidden noble, so toad also stands for a lowly outer form that hides something better.
senses.whyCN: 民间故事用这只寻常动物来伪装一位隐藏的高贵者，所以 toad 也代表「外表的低微掩藏着更好的东西」。

senses.title: Toadstool, a poisonous mushroom
senses.definition: the toad element in toadstool, the popular name for a mushroom thought to be poisonous
senses.definitionCN: toadstool 一词中的 toad 部分，是民间对有毒蘑菇的称呼
senses.example: Red toadstools grew in a ring among the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 红色的毒蘑菇在树间围成一圈生长。
senses.why: Old belief said toads sat on certain mushrooms and made them poisonous, so the animal name was joined to stool to name them.
senses.whyCN: 旧时认为蟾蜍会坐在某些蘑菇上使其带毒，于是把这种动物的名字和 stool（凳子）拼在一起命名。

intro.en: Toad is an English word of uncertain origin, generally compared with Dutch and German words for the same warty creature.
intro.cn: toad 是来源不确定的英语词，一般认为与荷兰语、德语中表示同种疙瘩皮动物的词同系。

items.en: Tadie and tadige name a warty jumping creature; the origin of the root is uncertain.
items.cn: 古英语 tadie、tadige 指一种皮肤起疙瘩的跳跃小动物；词根来源不确定。

items.en: Dutch and German forms such as padde and dotter are generally compared with the English word.
items.cn: 一般认为荷兰语 padde、德语 dotter 等词形与英语词同源。

items.en: The spelling settles as tode and later toad, still naming the animal alone.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 tode，后为 toad，仍只指这种动物。

items.en: Toadstool grows from toad plus stool, naming mushrooms folk belief linked with toads.
items.cn: toadstool 由 toad 加 stool 构成，指民间认为与蟾蜍有关的蘑菇。

items.en: Toady begins as the name of a hanger on who ate toads for a travelling quack.
items.cn: toady 起初指替江湖郎中吃蟾蜍的随从。

items.en: Modern English also uses toad for an ugly or spiteful person and for the frog of dry land.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 toad 指讨厌的人，以及旱地上的蛙类。

note.en: Toad belongs with its compounds toadstool and toady, and with the frog words it is always set against.
note.cn: toad 与复合词 toadstool、toady 同族，也总与它对照使用的青蛙类词相邻。

entries.definition: a mushroom that people believe is poisonous
a person who flatters others to win favour
something heavy that is carried
entries.definitionCN: 负载；只在拼写与读音上相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a jumping amphibian with smooth wet skin that lives near water
entries.definitionCN: 皮肤光滑湿润、常在水边生活的跳跃两栖动物，常与蟾蜍对照

entries.definition: an animal that can live both in water and on land
a small lizard-like amphibian that lives in or near water
entries.definitionCN: 水螈，一种体形像蜥蜴的小型两栖动物

normalIntro.en: Toad is the plain word for the warty land frog, and it grows compounds for mushrooms and flatterers.
normalIntro.cn: toad 是疙瘩皮旱蛙的朴素称呼，又长出表示毒蘑菇与谄媚者的复合词。

normal.en: Toad keeps the same shape in the plural, so toads are simply several of them.
normal.cn: toad 的复数只是加 s，toads 就是几只蟾蜍。

normal.en: Toadstool joins toad and stool, because folk belief put toads on mushrooms.
normal.cn: toadstool 把 toad 与 stool 拼在一起，因为民间认为蟾蜍会坐在蘑菇上。

normal.en: Toady is the flatterer who once ate toads for a quack.
normal.cn: toady 指当年替江湖郎中吃蟾蜍的谄媚随从。

normal.en: Toad and frog are a fixed pair: toad means dry skin and land, frog means wet skin and ponds.
normal.cn: toad 与 frog 是固定对照：toad 干燥、在旱地，frog 湿润、在池塘。

normal.en: Toadfish and toadlet keep the animal name for look-alikes, one a fish, one a tiny toad.
normal.cn: toadfish 与 toadlet 都借动物名指相似之物，一个是鱼，一个是小蟾蜍。

abstract.en: Picture a squat toad in a damp gap between stones, its skin covered with bumps.
abstract.cn: 想象一只矮胖的蟾蜍蹲在石头间的潮缝里，满身疙瘩。

abstract.en: Set a wet frog beside a dry toad on the same bank and note the two skins.
abstract.cn: 把湿漉漉的青蛙和干的蟾蜍并排放在同一岸边，注意两种皮肤。

abstract.en: See a red mushroom with a squat toad perched on its cap like a stool.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵红蘑菇，一只矮胖的蟾蜍像坐凳子一样趴在菌盖上。

examples.en: The toads emerge after warm rain and feed on insects.
examples.cn: 暖雨过后蟾蜍出来活动，捕食昆虫。

examples.en: Children in the village were warned never to eat a toadstool.
examples.cn: 村里的孩子都被告诫绝不要吃毒蘑菇。

examples.en: She called him a nasty old toad and walked out.
examples.cn: 她骂他是个讨厌的老家伙，转身走了出去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「透的」——蟾蜍皮肤粗糙起疙瘩，看着一点都不「透」，谐音正好反着记；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 tadie / tadige（皮肤起疙瘩的跳跃小动物）→ 中古英语 tode → toad。词根来源不确定，一般认为与荷兰语 padde、德语 dotter 等同系。

sensesIntro.en: Toad starts as the warty land frog, then contrasts with frog, extends to disliked people, to the enchanted prince of tales, and to the toad of toadstool.
sensesIntro.cn: toad 先指疙瘩皮的旱地蛙，再与 frog 对照，引申指讨厌的人、童话中受魔法变形的角色，以及 toadstool 里的那个 toad。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a squat toad with dry warty skin, sitting on damp ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只干皮疙瘩、矮胖蹲坐的蟾蜍趴在潮地上。

branches.en: The ordinary animal is the base sense.
branches.cn: 寻常的这种动物是基础义项。

branches.en: The dry land member of the frog pair is the contrast sense.
branches.cn: 与青蛙对照的旱地成员是对照义项。

branches.en: A rough ugly surface transferred to a person gives the insult.
branches.cn: 粗糙丑陋的外观转移到人身上，就有了贬称义。

branches.en: The plain animal becomes a disguise for a hidden prince in folktales.
branches.cn: 寻常动物在民间故事里成了隐藏王子的伪装。

branches.en: Folk belief links the animal with poisonous mushrooms, giving the compound toadstool.
branches.cn: 民间把这种动物与毒蘑菇联系起来，于是有了复合词 toadstool。

intro.en: Toad is a base noun of uncertain origin, and its English family runs from toadstool to toady.
intro.cn: toad 是来源不确定的基础名词，其英语词族从 toadstool 一直延伸到 toady。

latinIntro.en: Toad has no Latin ancestor and no Latin cognates, so only its English family is listed.
latinIntro.cn: toad 没有拉丁语来源，也没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁同源项。

items.meaningCN: 皮肤起疙瘩的跳跃小动物
items.example: Tadie is the earliest recorded form of the name.
items.exampleCN: tadie 是该词最早记录到的形式。

items.meaningCN: 疙瘩皮的旱地两栖动物
items.example: Toad is the modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: toad 是现代拼写。

items.example: The suffix -s forms toads.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 toads。

items.example: Stool joins toad to form toadstool.
items.exampleCN: stool 与 toad 合成 toadstool。

items.example: The suffix -let forms toadlet.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -let 构成 toadlet。

items.example: The suffix -like forms toadlike.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 toadlike。

items.example: Fish joins toad to form toadfish.
items.exampleCN: fish 与 toad 合成 toadfish。

items.meaningCN: 构成名词或形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -y helps form toady.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 参与构成 toady。

items.example: Toadstool carries folk belief into the word.
items.exampleCN: toadstool 把民间信仰带进了词里。

derivatives.zh: 由 toad 加 stool 构成，指有毒蘑菇
由 toad 加 -y 构成，指谄媚者
由 toad 加指小的 -let 构成，指小蟾蜍
